books.title: A Land Unknown
books.subtitle: America's New Machinery of Expulsion — and the Case for Ending It
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A man wins his case. An immigration judge finds that the government of his country would torture him, and forbids his removal there. Four years later he is put on an aircraft to a country he has never seen, handed to a warden who has no charge against him, and held in a prison built by somebody else's emergency.
Nobody broke the law. That is the problem.

A Land Unknown is the first full legal account of what the United States has built since 2025 - a triangular system of third-country removals, purchased detention, and confidential agreements in which the decision to expel is deliberately separated from responsibility for what follows. Drawing on the governing statutes, the 2025-2026 litigation, and the failed experiments of Britain, Australia, Canada and Italy, Dr. Zahir Hasan shows that the failures here are not administrative. They are the design.

Rigorous enough for a courtroom and written for anyone who has ever wondered what a border is actually for, this book ends where the evidence leads: not with a better procedure, but with a statute that would prohibit the practice outright.
For readers of immigration law, human rights, and American politics.

authorSite.blurb: America's New Machinery of Expulsion — and the Case for Ending It. A legal account of how people are removed to countries they have never seen, why nobody technically broke the law, and why that is the problem.

books.title: A Manufactured War
books.subtitle: The Israeli and American Assault on Iran
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: On 28 February 2026, American and Israeli aircraft struck Iran. Within hours the Supreme Leader was dead, the Strait of Hormuz was closing, and the world was pricing in the largest oil shock in history. Governments called it necessity. This book calls it a choice.

A Manufactured War traces how three decades of warnings, the deliberate dismantling of the nuclear deal, and the domestic troubles of two embattled leaders converged to produce a war that experts had long predicted — and that diplomacy had nearly prevented just days before the first strikes.

This edition is updated through August 2026, adding six new chapters and more than thirteen thousand words. They follow the collapse of the Islamabad talks and the naval blockade that came after; the fourteen-point memorandum signed at Versailles and the ambiguities that unravelled it within a fortnight; the contested succession inside Iran after Khamenei’s killing; the economic damage, now measured rather than forecast, from Dhaka to Berlin; the unanswered constitutional question of who may take a country to war; and the summer of attrition in which a conflict neither government calls a war has quietly become permanent. A dated chronology runs from the 2015 nuclear deal to the present.

Drawing on parliamentary briefings, government documents, and research from across the region — fully referenced throughout — this is a clear, unflinching account for students of policy, for investors, and for every reader who wants to understand how avoidable wars are made, and how they might be made harder.

authorSite.blurb: How conflicts are constructed, sustained, and sold — and who benefits from the stories we are told about war.

books.title: Asia Between Giants
books.subtitle: America, China, and the Contest for the Region
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The two most powerful countries on earth are contesting a region that neither can leave. America has stood in the Western Pacific since 1945. China now has the ships, the missiles, the factories, and the will to push back. Between them sit Japan, Korea, Taiwan, the Philippines, and the six hundred million people of Southeast Asia who would rather not choose.

Asia Between Giants sets out what the contest is about, measures both sides without flattery, and walks the map where a crisis could turn into a war: the Taiwan Strait, the shoals of the South China Sea, the Korean Peninsula, and the islands of southern Japan. It weighs the instruments each side is using, tariffs and truces, chips and rare earths, missiles and warheads, loans and narratives, and asks which of them actually work. It tests the explanations on offer against the record of the Trump and Xi years, and it ends where a book like this should: with the choices, compared on clear criteria, and the recommendations that follow for Washington, for Beijing, and for the countries in between.

Written for readers who want the facts in order and the argument made plainly, it is a book about avoiding the war that would ruin everyone, and about why the region, not the two capitals, may decide whether that war happens.

authorSite.blurb: The two most powerful countries on earth are contesting a region that neither can leave. America has stood in the Western Pacific since 1945. China now has the ships, the missiles, the factories, and the will to push back.

books.title: Black Companies in Japan
books.subtitle: Unpaid Overtime, Overwork, and the Struggle for Labour Justice
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Japan’s so-called black companies are not a curiosity of workplace culture. They show how sales targets, insecure jobs, doctored time records, harassment, and weak worker voice can turn ordinary management systems into engines of unpaid labour and harm.

Drawing on current law, official inspection and compensation data, peer-reviewed research, and carefully delimited corporate cases, Black Companies in Japan explains how exploitation operates, why enforcement so often arrives late, and what a credible labour-justice agenda requires. It distinguishes the social label from the legal record, reads Japan’s enforcement statistics with their denominators attached, and follows the harm from unpaid hours to karōshi.

The final part turns to the person inside the system. A practical guide for workers shows how to read a job advertisement, keep the working-time log that wins wage claims, calculate what is owed, write the demand letter, use the Labour Standards Inspection Office and the labour tribunal, document harassment, and resign from a company that will not let you go. Every step comes with a fully worked model rather than a blank form, and the book closes with a verified directory of free, multilingual help.

Nine original figures and eleven analytical tables. Sixty-three references in APA style. For students of Japanese labour, managers and HR professionals, policy-makers, and anyone who suspects that their employer is taking more than it pays for.

authorSite.blurb: Japan’s so-called black companies are not a curiosity of workplace culture. They show how sales targets, insecure jobs, doctored time records, harassment, and weak worker voice can turn ordinary management systems into engines of unpaid labour and harm.

books.title: Canada at the Crossroads
books.subtitle: Multiculturalism, Allegiance, and the Meaning of Citizenship
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Can a country be generous without being naive?

Canada's official multiculturalism policy has always invited a hard question: can a country protect cultural heritage without weakening the shared civic life that makes it governable? For decades the comfortable answer was yes. That answer no longer comes easily.

Drawing on Statistics Canada data, the findings of the Hogue Commission on foreign interference, current polling on Canadian public opinion, and a wide body of research on immigrant integration, Quebec nationalism, and Indigenous rights, Canada at the Crossroads argues that the country's diversity remains workable — but only if paired with a renewed civic compact: real credential recognition for skilled immigrants, transparent public spending, immigration levels matched to housing and service capacity, and a security posture that protects targeted communities rather than treating them as suspects.

Neither a celebration of multiculturalism nor an obituary for it, this book takes seriously both the strongest case for the policy and the strongest case against it — then asks what Canada must actually do, starting now, to keep its bargain with itself.

Written by a Canadian-born public policy, law, and education scholar, Canada at the Crossroads includes a glossary, a timeline of Canadian multiculturalism policy since Confederation, discussion questions for book clubs and classrooms, and 34 fully cited sources with URLs and DOIs.

authorSite.blurb: Can a country be generous without being naive?

books.title: Canada’s European Option
books.subtitle: Associate Membership, Sovereignty, and Strategy in a Fragmenting World
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: On September 16, 2026, the European Commission president proposed opening the door for Canada to become the European Union’s first associate member. The invitation was historic, but the new status came without a rulebook. What would Canada gain? What obligations would it accept? And can it diversify without damaging its indispensable relationship with the United States?

Canada’s European Option provides a clear, evidence-based answer. Zahir Hasan examines the legal routes to association, the unfinished work of CETA, and Canada’s growing participation in Horizon Europe, the EU’s SAFE defence instrument, and European security forums. He then turns to the practical agenda: trade, energy, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, the Arctic, defence production, mobility, infrastructure, and the political obstacles within both Canada and the EU.

The book recommends a staged Atlantic Association built on reciprocal access, explicit obligations, parliamentary oversight, provincial and Indigenous participation, and measurable results. A closing chapter tests that recommendation against the alternatives, the strongest objections, and the costs, and states the conditions under which the advice should change. It rejects both dependence on one partner and the illusion that Europe can replace the United States. The path forward is strategic pluralism: stronger capacity at home and several durable partnerships abroad.
Timely and practical, this book is for readers seeking to understand how a new Canada-EU relationship could reshape trade, security, and sovereignty in a fragmenting world.

authorSite.blurb: On September 16, 2026, the European Commission president proposed opening the door for Canada to become the European Union’s first associate member. The invitation was historic, but the new status came without a rulebook. What would Canada gain? What obligations would it accept?

books.title: Duty of Care
books.subtitle: Big Tech, Children, and the Battle to Make Social Media Safe
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Who builds the room children enter?

On August 26, 2026, a federal judge in Oakland approved a court-ordered overhaul of Instagram and Facebook for teenagers: default time limits, a midnight lockout, quiet hours during school, and payments of up to $17.1 billion. It was the most concrete answer yet to a question that parents, engineers, whistleblowers, scientists and judges had fought over for a decade.

Duty of Care tells that story through the people who lived it: the designers who built the endless feed and later regretted it, the engineer who wrote to Mark Zuckerberg about his own daughter, the whistleblower who carried internal research to Congress, the parents who held up photographs in a Senate hearing room, and the state investigators who created a fictional 13-year-old to see what a platform would send her.

It follows the law as it caught up, from Section 230 and the children's privacy law of 1998 to the Los Angeles and New Mexico verdicts and the Oakland consent judgment, read term by term. It weighs the scientific evidence fairly, keeping allegation apart from finding, and it compares the very different paths taken by Britain, the European Union, Australia, Canada and Japan.

Then it turns practical. The book sets out a ten-part duty of care standard and a Toolkit of complete, filled-in models: a youth safety impact assessment, a 90-day platform plan, a family media agreement, a school response protocol for sextortion, a public audit scorecard, model legislative language, ten questions to ask before believing a safety announcement, and an implementation register for the Oakland settlement.
For parents, teachers, school leaders, policymakers, lawyers and anyone who builds technology that children use.

authorSite.blurb: Who builds the room children enter? On August 26, 2026, a federal judge in Oakland approved a court-ordered overhaul of Instagram and Facebook for teenagers: default time limits, a midnight lockout, quiet hours during school, and payments of up to $17.1 billion.

books.title: Elbows Up
books.subtitle: Canada, the United States, and the Rupture of a Continental Partnership
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The tariffs were justified by a number that was wrong by a factor of ten.

Between January 2025 and August 2026, the United States imposed the most severe tariff regime on Canadian goods of the postwar era, saw its legal foundation struck down by its own Supreme Court, rebuilt it within four days, and then reached back ninety-six years to invoke a provision of the Tariff Act of 1930 that no president had ever used. Throughout, the President of the United States said publicly that Canada should cease to exist as a country.

Elbows Up is the first full account of that rupture, and it is built entirely from primary sources: Statistics Canada, the Bank of Canada, the Parliamentary Budget Officer, the U.S. Census Bureau, the Energy Information Administration, the Federal Reserve, the Congressional Research Service, and the Supreme Court itself.

Its central finding is arithmetic. The United States did not subsidize Canada by $200 billion a year. The combined goods-and-services deficit in 2025 was roughly $20.6 billion; seven one-hundredths of one percent of American output. Strip out a single commodity, heavy crude oil sold to American refiners at a structural discount, and the United States ran a surplus with Canada of roughly $64 billion.

Dr. Zahir Hasan states his standpoint openly and then argues from evidence an opponent cannot dispute. He concedes Canada's thirty years of defence free-riding, the indefensible administration of its dairy quotas, and the uncomfortable fact that Canada's celebrated export diversification was, in 2025, largely the price of gold.
What emerges is not a lament. It is a reckoning; with Washington, and with a country that knew its own vulnerability in detail and would not act on it until somebody made acting unavoidable.
Includes: a full chronology of the trade war, ten data tables, a glossary, and complete APA references.

authorSite.blurb: Canada, the United States, and the Rupture of a Continental Partnership. How the deepest trade relationship of the postwar era came apart between 2025 and 2026 — and what the break means for both countries.

books.title: Is It Time to End the United Nations?
books.subtitle: Power, Legitimacy, and the Future of Collective Security
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: In one week of September 2026 the General Assembly heard the president of a permanent member weigh aloud whether to annihilate another member's government, and, two days later, a prime minister wanted by the International Criminal Court. Seven months earlier the Security Council had condemned Iran's retaliation for the strikes that began the war, and never once voted on the strikes themselves.

Is it time to end the United Nations? Zahir Hasan asks the question in earnest. He follows the idea of world organization from the Concert of Europe to the League of Nations' last Assembly in Geneva, shows how the veto was priced and paid for at Yalta and San Francisco, and reads the record of the last decade, Gaza, Ukraine, Sudan, the Iran war, the money and the machine, against the condition the founders themselves wrote down in 1945: that an organization unable to keep the peace, or able to keep it only at the expense of law and justice, should expect to be dissolved.

His answer is not yet, and not like that. The book proposes a Second Charter, drafted by a General Conference under Article 109 of the Charter, the one route to reform that the veto cannot block, with a fixed date for the five permanent members to accept it or be left behind, and a calendar that runs from 2027 to 2031. It tests the design against the vetoes of the last decade, and the model texts, including a complete draft resolution and draft treaty articles, are in the appendices.
Fifteen chapters, four appendices, more than 570 sources, research current to 26 September 2026.

authorSite.blurb: In one week of September 2026 the General Assembly heard the president of a permanent member weigh aloud whether to annihilate another member's government, and, two days later, a prime minister wanted by the International Criminal Court.

books.title: Japan's Secret War
books.subtitle: Spies, Scandals, and the Fight to Build a Modern Intelligence State
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: On July 31, 2026, Japan quietly dismantled the intelligence office it had deliberately kept weak for eighty years, and replaced it with something it had never had before. A new National Intelligence Council, backed by a National Intelligence Bureau with real legal authority to compel Japan's own agencies to share what they know, took over from the modest Cabinet Intelligence and Research Office that morning — the most significant change to Japan's national security architecture since 1945.

Japan's Secret War tells the full story behind that reform, starting not in 2026 but in 1901, and following Japan's intelligence history through the Tokko's reign of political terror, Richard Sorge's penetration of wartime Tokyo, the postwar occupation, three Cold War-era scandals, the crises of the 1990s, and thirteen years of legislative guardrail-building. Written by a Tokyo-based university teacher with graduate training in public policy, law, and education, the book gives a fair hearing to the strongest arguments against the reform as well as for it, and asks whether Japan's democracy has built the tools to judge its own creation.

authorSite.blurb: On July 31, 2026, Japan quietly dismantled the intelligence office it had deliberately kept weak for eighty years, and replaced it with something it had never had before.

books.title: Japan's Strategic Awakening
books.subtitle: Law, Capability, and the Realignment of Indo-Pacific Security
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Can a nation built for peace defend it? For nearly eighty years, Japan kept the peace through a careful bargain: a pacifist constitution, American protection, and a stable Asia. That bargain is breaking. Chinese coast guard fleets circle disputed islands. North Korean missiles arc over Japanese towns. Russian and Chinese warships sail the archipelago in company. And in Washington, old certainties are giving way to hard bargaining.
Japan's Strategic Awakening tells the story of how the world's most successful pacifist democracy is answering: record defense budgets, counterstrike missiles,
historic warship exports to Australia, a lattice of new partnerships across the Indo-Pacific—and a constitutional question that can no longer be deferred.

Writing from Tokyo, Dr. Zahir Hasan examines the law, the capabilities, and the alliances behind Japan's transformation, and argues that peace endures only when all three align. Includes a chronology, glossary, discussion questions for classroom use, and full APA references. Essential reading for students of international relations, policy professionals, and anyone who wants to understand the future of Asia.

authorSite.blurb: Law, Capability, and the Realignment of Indo-Pacific Security. An analysis of Japan's evolving security posture and the strategic choices reshaping the Indo-Pacific.

books.title: Japan’s Unavoidable Choice
books.subtitle: Immigration, Artificial Intelligence, and the Struggle to Remain a Global Power
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Can Japan remain a major global power while its population and workforce steadily decline?

Japan faces a defining choice. It can continue limiting permanent immigration and place its faith in artificial intelligence, robotics, and a smaller but more productive society. Or it can reconsider how foreign workers, long-term residents, and future citizens fit into the nation’s economic and strategic future.

Japan’s Unavoidable Choice examines the relationship between demographic decline, immigration policy, artificial intelligence, care shortages, public finance, regional contraction, and national security. It also considers a central geopolitical question: whether Japan can preserve its influence as China becomes more powerful in Asia and throughout the world.
Drawing on Japanese government data, international institutions, and peer-reviewed research, the book explores:

Why Japan’s population decline cannot be solved by technology alone? What robots and artificial intelligence can—and cannot—replace? How temporary foreign-worker programs affect productivity and human rights? What Japan can learn from South Korea, Taiwan, Germany, Canada, and Singapore? How demographic decline affects defense, alliances, and competition with China? Four possible versions of Japan in 2050.
The book concludes with a practical ten-year strategy combining automation, domestic labor reform, managed immigration, fiscal adjustment, and carefully planned regional adaptation.
A timely and evidence-based examination of what Japan must change to preserve what matters most.

authorSite.blurb: Immigration, Artificial Intelligence, and the Struggle to Remain a Global Power. Can Japan stay a major power while its population declines? On a choice the country can no longer postpone.

books.title: NATO at the Breaking Point
books.subtitle: War in Ukraine, American Uncertainty, and the Future of European Security
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: NATO has never been stronger on paper — and never more exposed in practice.

Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the Alliance has rearmed, expanded, and rediscovered the seriousness of territorial defense. Finland and Sweden have joined. Defense budgets are climbing toward a historic 5% of GDP. Eastern-flank battlegroups have grown from four to nine. And yet the hardest question NATO faces isn’t whether it has enough power — it plainly does — but whether it can move that power to the right place fast enough, before a limited attack becomes a fait accompli.

Drawing on official NATO and national strategy documents, defense-spending data, legislative and audit reports, and the record of the war in Ukraine, this book argues that NATO’s real vulnerability is temporal: the danger sits in the gap between announced spending and delivered capability, between summit unity and the ability to act under surprise. It examines the infrastructure that deterrence actually depends on — railways, fuel networks, repair capacity, industrial contracts — and the gray-zone and infrastructure attacks already testing it. It confronts an American security strategy that now asks Europe to lead its own defense. And it steelmans the strongest objections to its own argument before answering them.

NATO at the Breaking Point is not a case for alarm or for complacency. It is a diagnosis — of where deterrence may fail, and what can still be measured and changed before a crisis tests the Alliance for real.

authorSite.blurb: War in Ukraine, American Uncertainty, and the Future of European Security. NATO has never looked stronger on paper, or been more exposed in practice — on the hard questions now facing the Alliance.

books.title: Neighbors Who Cannot Move
books.subtitle: Japan, China, and the End of the 1972 Bargain
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: On November 7, 2025, Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae answered a question about Taiwan in a committee room in Tokyo. Within weeks China had warned its citizens away from Japan, halted Japanese seafood imports, tightened exports of rare earths and dual-use goods, and demanded a retraction that never came.

Zahir Hasan argues that the quarrel exposed a settlement built in 1972 for a world that has vanished: a poor China beside a rich Japan, a predictable America, and a sea that neither side could yet patrol day after day. All three conditions are gone. Tracing the story from the Treaty of Shimonoseki to the fire-control radar incident of December 2025, he shows how ambiguity kept the peace for half a century and why it can no longer do so on its own.

Neither nostalgia nor confrontation will serve. The book makes the case for defended coexistence: credible defense and civil resilience, precise legal language, targeted economic security instead of decoupling, and crisis rules that hold even when the two governments are not speaking.

Drawing on the scholarly literature, official records from Tokyo and Beijing, and events through mid-October 2026, Neighbors Who Cannot Move is a clear, argued guide for students, policy readers, and anyone who wants to understand the most important relationship in Asia.

authorSite.blurb: On November 7, 2025, Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae answered a question about Taiwan in a committee room in Tokyo.

books.title: Pakistan's Unfinished Democratic Transition
books.subtitle: Military Tutelage, Institutional Weakness, and the Search for Civilian Supremacy
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: No prime minister of Pakistan has ever finished a term.

Generals have governed Pakistan outright for roughly a third of its life and shaped it for most of the rest. The familiar explanations — ambitious commanders, corrupt politicians, American interference — are each partly right and jointly inadequate.

In this study, Zahir Hasan argues that the binding constraint on Pakistan's democracy is not the strength of its army but the army's autonomy from constitutional control: an autonomy sustained by weak parties, obliging courts, an opaque military economy, and foreign partners who prefer one reliable interlocutor to a noisy parliament. He traces the pattern from the abrogation of the 1956 Constitution through the loss of East Pakistan, the Zia and Musharraf years, and the hybrid order that followed 2018 — and he states the strongest objections to his own case before answering them.

Is Pakistan a failed state? No — and the true answer is harder to live with. It is a state that is powerful and weak at once: able to confront a nuclear-armed rival and unable to tax its wealthiest sectors, formidable against a journalist and helpless against a flood.

Drawing on democratic transitions in Indonesia, Turkey, Chile, and South Korea, the book closes with a sequenced program for civilian supremacy in which every reform carries an instrument, an owner, and a public test.
Fully referenced in APA 7 style, with a 1947–2026 chronology, a guide to Pakistan's institutions and parties, and forty-nine case boxes.

authorSite.blurb: Military Tutelage, Institutional Weakness, and the Search for Civilian Supremacy. No prime minister of Pakistan has ever finished a term — an inquiry into why, and into what civilian supremacy would actually take.

books.title: Taiwan at the Fault Line
books.subtitle: Deterrence, Alliance, and the Struggle to Keep the Peace in the Indo-Pacific
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Can deterrence hold across the Taiwan Strait—without tipping into the war it is meant to prevent? Taiwan sits at the meeting point of history, geography, technology, and alliance politics—and a crisis there would reach far beyond the Strait. Coercion short of war, the credibility of American and allied commitments, the fragility of semiconductor supply chains, and the risk that preparation itself is mistaken for provocation: these are the fault lines this book maps. Dr. Zahir Hasan examines the uncertainties that most shape outcomes—escalation management, alliance decision-making in Washington and Tokyo, economic resilience, and the limits of analogies to Ukraine and past crises. Drawing on defense white papers, treaty law, and current scholarship on deterrence theory, he argues that peace in the Indo-Pacific depends on visible preparation before a crisis, not promises made after one has begun. Written for policymakers, students of international security, and general readers alike, Taiwan at the Fault Line does not predict war. It makes the case for taking the peace seriously enough to prepare for it.

authorSite.blurb: Can deterrence hold across the Taiwan Strait—without tipping into the war it is meant to prevent?

books.title: The AI Advantage
books.subtitle: How China Could Overtake the West in AI Models, Services, and Digital Power
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Artificial intelligence is usually scored at the frontier: the strongest model, the newest chips, the largest training run. This book argues that a second contest may matter more — and that the West may be winning the first while losing the second.

The AI Advantage follows the technology out of the laboratory and into the places where power becomes tangible: a data center waiting on a substation, a factory line where a vision model must earn its keep, a finance ministry weighing a cheap local model against an expensive foreign one, a courtroom deciding what a model may be trained on.

Zahir Hasan weighs China's route to practical influence — efficient models, open weights, manufacturing depth, super-app distribution and aggressive pricing — against its real constraints in semiconductors, capital, debt, demography and trust. He asks the harder question of the West: whether frontier leadership can be converted into broad, affordable, correctable use, or whether it will be wasted on weak diffusion, unstable policy and scarce power.
Evidence-based and current through September 2026, drawing on official policy documents, company filings, regulators and independent measurement, with 389 cited sources.

authorSite.blurb: Artificial intelligence is usually scored at the frontier: the strongest model, the newest chips, the largest training run. This book argues that a second contest may matter more — and that the West may be winning the first while losing the second.

books.title: The AI Slowdown Paradox
books.subtitle: Safety, Competition and the Battle Over Who Controls the Pace of Intelligence
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Four people who pay every month for artificial intelligence have sued the four companies that sell it to them. The injury they allege is that the products are getting better too slowly.

In September 2026, a consumer class action accused Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google of agreeing to slow the improvement of their assistants in the name of safety. Antitrust law does not let competitors decide among themselves that competition has become too dangerous to continue. But the danger they cite may be real, and no government anywhere currently has the legal power to make a frontier AI developer slow down.

Zahir Hasan follows that conflict through competition law, consumer economics, labour and education, energy and chips, national security, and the comparative record of aviation, nuclear power, medicine and chemicals, where rivals have cooperated on safety for decades without becoming a cartel. He argues for a public safety floor set by law, independent evaluation with real access, narrow and supervised information sharing, and unrestricted competition above the floor.
The central conflict is not speed against safety. It is private power against legitimate control over speed.

authorSite.blurb: Four people who pay every month for artificial intelligence have sued the four companies that sell it to them. The injury they allege is that the products are getting better too slowly.

books.title: The Arab Dilemma
books.subtitle: Gaza, Atrocity, and the Politics of Abandonment After October 7
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Why did the world watch Gaza's destruction unfold — and look away?

On October 7, 2023, Hamas's attack on Israel set in motion a war whose scale of devastation in Gaza has been called, by many observers, an overkill. The Arab Dilemma asks the harder question that followed: why did Arab governments — bound to Palestinians by language, faith, and decades of solidarity rhetoric — largely stand aside? And why did the wider international community, despite mounting evidence of atrocity, fail to stop it?

Drawing on international law, diplomatic history, and the shifting politics of the Middle East, Dr. Zahir Hasan traces the political calculations, historical grievances, and strategic interests behind this collective abandonment. Chapter by chapter, the book examines the actions — and inactions — of Egypt, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Iran, and the Gulf states, then widens the lens to the United Nations, the United States, and Europe.

This is not a one-sided polemic. Hasan holds human rights violations to a single standard, weighing the brutality of October 7 alongside the scale of Gaza's destruction, and confronts uncomfortable truths on every side of the conflict. The book closes with forward-looking, actionable recommendations for regional and international policymakers — written as the conflict continues and peace proposals are repeatedly rejected.
For readers of Middle East politics, international relations, and human rights history who want an analytical, evidence-based account — not another op-ed.
Zahir Hasan holds graduate degrees in public policy, law, and education, and teaches at the university level in Tokyo.

authorSite.blurb: Gaza, Atrocity, and the Politics of Abandonment After October 7. Why did Arab governments — long bound to the Palestinian cause — watch Gaza's destruction and look away?

books.title: The Breaking of American Democracy
books.subtitle: Power, Profit, and the Unmaking of Constitutional Restraint
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: What happens when the safeguards around public power weaken while private financial interests remain close to the presidency?

*The Breaking of American Democracy* is an evidence-based examination of conflict-of-interest risk, executive power, congressional oversight, and the constitutional guardrails designed to protect the public trust. Dr. Zahir Hasan traces the institutional precedents of the first Trump administration through the second administration’s evolving ethics framework, reported financial disclosures, family-business networks, personnel choices, and the Supreme Court’s presidential-immunity doctrine.

Drawing on court opinions, congressional materials, government reports, financial disclosures, and contemporaneous journalism, the book distinguishes documented facts, allegations, legal holdings, denials, and analysis. It does not treat every troubling claim as proved. Instead, it asks a more durable democratic question: what institutions must exist for citizens to know whether private interest is influencing public power?

This work of documented political nonfiction argues that democratic decline is often incremental. It appears in delayed records, weakened independent oversight, opaque financial relationships, politicized accountability, and a growing belief that political power can shield itself from ordinary legal constraint. It also offers a practical framework for repair.

authorSite.blurb: What happens when the safeguards around public power weaken while private financial interests remain close to the presidency?

books.title: The Broken Periphery
books.subtitle: Turkey, Israel, and the Problem of Regional Order
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: For half a century, Turkey and Israel were the Middle East's unlikely partners: two outsiders who found each other useful. Turkey recognized Israel in 1949. In the 1990s their militaries signed cooperation agreements, their pilots trained together over Anatolia, and trade boomed. Today Turkish and Israeli forces operate across Syria, Iranian missiles have streaked toward Turkish airspace, and the two governments trade charges of genocide and empire.

What broke the periphery? Zahir Hasan begins from first principles: what states want, how power works, and why fear feeds on itself. Drawing on scholarship, official records, and reporting through October 2026, he shows how three forces broke the partnership together: politics at home in both countries, the war in Gaza and the Palestinian question behind it, and the collapse of the states that once stood between Turkish and Israeli power.
Inside you will find:
• The full history, from the 1949 recognition and the secret periphery pact to the golden decade of the 1990s, the Mavi Marmara, and the repair that almost happened in 2023
• The great rupture of 2023 to 2026: Gaza, the trade embargo that leaks, the collision in Syria, the wars with Iran, and the contest over the Eastern Mediterranean
• A clear-eyed account of Israel's military reach and its costs, and of Turkey's industrial rise and its dependence on NATO
• An evidence ledger in every narrative chapter separating what is established from what is still uncertain
• Critical tests of the popular explanations, a panel of seven expert perspectives, four scenarios to 2030, and a decision analysis of six options
• A concrete program of managed rivalry, with model texts for an incident-prevention memorandum and a joint statement on restoring ambassadors

Balanced, accessible, and practical, The Broken Periphery is for students, diplomats, analysts, investors, and citizens who want to understand one of the most dangerous rivalries in the Middle East, and what can be done about it.

authorSite.blurb: For half a century, Turkey and Israel were the Middle East's unlikely partners: two outsiders who found each other useful. Turkey recognized Israel in 1949. In the 1990s their militaries signed cooperation agreements, their pilots trained together over Anatolia, and trade boomed.

books.title: The Last Island of Paper
books.subtitle: The Eccentric Economists, Stubborn Artisans, and Quiet Revolutionaries Fighting the Death of Physical Currency
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Money used to have a body. Somebody is trying to keep it alive.

In a windowless fortress in France, a sixty-four-year-old engraver carves lines into steel that no scanner can copy. In a basement laboratory, a neuroeconomist pays volunteers to feel the small, measurable sting of handing over cash. In Stockholm, a retired policeman fights a country that abolished money without ever voting on it. In Zurich, a man in a cardigan keeps a fortune in thousand-franc notes because he is afraid of a Tuesday. And in a central bank, a mild public servant shows the author the future of money: a box on a screen where you can type a rule.

The Last Island of Paper is a journey through the strange, stubborn world of the people who still know what money feels like—engravers, campaigners, tollbooth operators, family-office managers, financial-crime investigators, and the designers of programmable currency—and a report from the places where the paper has already gone: the Swedish supermarket that will not take kronor, the Indian queues of November 2016, the Spanish town where the lights went out and only a biscuit tin of notes still worked.
It is a book about convenience, and what convenience costs. It is a book about the last room in the economy with no camera in it.

authorSite.blurb: Money used to have a body. Somebody is trying to keep it alive. In a windowless fortress in France, a sixty-four-year-old engraver carves lines into steel that no scanner can copy.

books.title: The Loss of Goodwill
books.subtitle: Israel, Gaza, and the Crisis of Moral Legitimacy
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The Loss of Goodwill is a documented history and legal analysis of how a state founded on the moral urgency of Jewish refuge came to face allegations of apartheid, forced displacement, and genocide.

Zahir Hasan traces the arc from the Holocaust and the founding of Israel through the Nakba, the 1967 occupation, Oslo, settlement and de facto annexation, the blockade of Gaza, the atrocities of October 7, 2023, and the war that followed. This edition carries the record through the ceasefire of October 2025 and its unfinished aftermath, the regional war fought in Lebanon, Syria, and Iran, the arms restrictions and trade measures imposed by Israel’s own allies, and the argument now under way inside Jewish communities about what memory requires.

The book is built on primary sources: orders and advisory opinions of the International Court of Justice, warrants and rulings of the International Criminal Court, United Nations investigations, peer-reviewed mortality studies, Israeli government arguments in their own words, archival scholarship, and international polling. It separates documented fact from allegation, provisional measures from final judgments, and legal finding from moral judgment.

It condemns Hamas’s crimes, rejects collective blame and Nazi analogies, and insists that Jewish safety and Palestinian freedom are not rival claims to humanity. It asks a harder question: can security remain legitimate when it depends on another people’s permanent subordination?

authorSite.blurb: The Loss of Goodwill is a documented history and legal analysis of how a state founded on the moral urgency of Jewish refuge came to face allegations of apartheid, forced displacement, and genocide.

books.title: The New American Witch Hunt
books.subtitle: Science, Covid, and the Criminalization of Dissent in the Trump Era
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A subpoena is not a verdict.

In September 2026, federal agents and prosecutors were seeking phone records, grant files and grand-jury testimony from at least eight scientists. One of them was Anthony Fauci. Another was a Nobel laureate whose only visible link to the case was a letter he had organized six years earlier.

Zahir Hasan takes both halves of the story seriously. A senior NIH official really did plead guilty to concealing federal records. Oversight of the Wuhan research funding really did fail. The origin of SARS-CoV-2 really is unresolved, and a laboratory incident cannot be ruled out. None of that, he argues, establishes the political story that has been built on top of it.

The New American Witch Hunt is an account of how legitimate accountability turns into something else — when officials announce the verdict before the evidence, when association replaces individual conduct, and when the process itself becomes the punishment. Working from court filings, audits, declassified intelligence, the Senate hearing transcript and the peer-reviewed literature, it separates four questions that public argument keeps collapsing into one: where the virus came from, whether American institutions supervised risky research properly, whether anyone committed a crime, and whether the government is now investigating people for what they said rather than what they did.

It is not a defense of anyone. A full chapter is given to the official who pleaded guilty, and a full appendix to the strongest case against the book's own thesis. What it refuses to do is let one man's admitted misconduct lower the standard of proof for everyone standing near him.

Includes a full chronology from grant to grand jury, a reader's guide to weighing the evidence, a claim-by-claim assessment of the origins debate, a ten-point institutional reform agenda, and four documentary case files.

authorSite.blurb: A subpoena is not a verdict. In September 2026, federal agents and prosecutors were seeking phone records, grant files and grand-jury testimony from at least eight scientists. One of them was Anthony Fauci.

books.title: The People’s House and the Free Press
books.subtitle: Trump, White House Access, and the First Amendment
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A president may condemn journalism as fiercely as he likes. That is politics. When the White House switches off a credential because it dislikes the coverage, the question stops being political and becomes constitutional.

On a Friday afternoon in September 2026, the President of the United States announced that CNN, MS NOW and Politico were banned from the White House. The next morning their correspondents arrived at the gate and found that their passes no longer worked.

Zahir Hasan follows that question from Robert Sherrill's refused pass in 1977, through Jim Acosta, Brian Karem and Simon Ateba, to the Associated Press and its fight over two words on a map — an appeal the D.C. Circuit had still not decided when this book closed.

He walks the White House room by room, from the briefing room to Air Force One, and shows why the constitutional answer changes as you move. He traces the quarrel back through Nixon, Kennedy, Roosevelt, Wilson, Lincoln and the Sedition Act of 1798, and he is as unsparing about the Obama administration's treatment of Fox News as about the present one.

The government's strongest case is set out in full before it is answered. The verdict that follows is calibrated rather than shouted: no newsroom is owed a seat at every table, but criticism cannot lawfully become the price of admission.
A rule that protects only the press you happen to like is not a rule at all.
An evidence-led account for lawyers, journalists, students of American government, and anyone who wants to know what the First Amendment actually requires when a president closes a gate.

authorSite.blurb: A president may condemn journalism as fiercely as he likes. That is politics. When the White House switches off a credential because it dislikes the coverage, the question stops being political and becomes constitutional.

books.title: The Permanent Suspect
books.subtitle: Islamophobia's Long Run Through North American Life
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A caricature does not survive contact with a person.

For more than two decades, North American news, film, and policy have taught millions of people to recognize Muslims as a threat before recognizing them as neighbors. The Permanent Suspect traces how that habit of mind was built — and how it endures.

The story begins before September 11, 2001, in the older Orientalist imagery that primed audiences to see the Muslim world as backward and threatening. It follows the post-9/11 security state as it hardened that imagery into policy: watchlists, secondary screening, surveillance programs, and travel bans that fell disproportionately on Muslim citizens and immigrants. It tracks how Hollywood convention, and later streaming-era algorithms, kept the caricature in circulation long after the headlines moved on. And it follows the same pattern north of the border, through Quebec's Bill 21, the Quebec City mosque shooting, and Canada's own security and immigration apparatus.

Grounded in court filings, government reports, peer-reviewed research, and named, dated events rather than appeals to feeling alone, The Permanent Suspect insists throughout on a rigorous, checkable standard of evidence. It does not ask readers to take fear or grievance on faith — it shows its sources, and lets the record speak.

The book argues for a simple, exacting standard: that belonging in a democratic society is not a feeling extended by the goodwill of a majority, but a public practice, sustained or withheld by specific, nameable institutional choices — in newsrooms, in writers' rooms, in legislatures, and in security agencies.

Written for readers of history, media criticism, and civil rights — and for anyone who has ever been asked to prove, once again, that they belong — The Permanent Suspect is a documented account of how a community was made permanently suspect, and what it would take to undo it.

authorSite.blurb: An examination of how suspicion becomes permanent — and what that means for justice, identity, and the state.

books.title: The Politics of Removal
books.subtitle: Imran Khan, Law, Sovereignty, and Pakistan’s Hybrid Order
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The first prime minister Pakistan ever removed by a vote. What happened next is the real story.

On 10 April 2022, Imran Khan became the first prime minister in Pakistan’s history to be removed by a no-confidence vote. What followed was extraordinary even by the standards of Pakistani politics: a cascade of prosecutions—cipher, Toshakhana, iddat, Al-Qadir Trust—that put a former prime minister behind bars while his movement won the most seats in a national election.

The Politics of Removal is an evidence-led examination of that story. Distinguishing established fact from allegation and from editorial judgment, it asks what the sequencing and density of the cases against Khan reveal about law’s coercive power in a hybrid regime—and what their use has cost the institutions that wielded them.

Neither prosecution nor hagiography, the book weighs the strongest counterarguments—Khan’s own polarizing politics, genuine accountability interests, and the constitutional basis of the vote that removed him. Updated through July 2026, with a complete chronology of the court cases and a fully sourced record.
Zahir Hasan (MPPA, LLM, EdD) is a Canadian academic who teaches at the university level in Tokyo.

authorSite.blurb: An inquiry into displacement, exclusion, and the political logic that decides who belongs and who is removed.

books.title: The Proof Machine
books.subtitle: Artificial Intelligence and the New Battle Over Mathematical Truth
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: In the autumn of 2026, machines began producing mathematics faster than people could read it.

Over Labor Day weekend, ten thousand AI agents worked for 88 hours on one of the Clay Institute's million-dollar Millennium Prize problems, and OpenAI announced a solution. The night before, a mathematician in New York had posted a statement about closely related results of his own. A month later the company released more than seven hundred mathematical manuscripts in a single day. Then two rival laboratories reported that their machines had refuted a hypothesis on which a whole branch of computer science had rested for more than twenty years.

Proofs had suddenly become cheap. Everything that has to happen after a proof is written had not: someone still has to check it, understand it, decide who deserves the credit, and work out what can safely be built on top of it.

The Proof Machine follows the people who found themselves holding those jobs: eminent mathematicians asked to examine a machine's refutation of their own conjecture, researchers in London and Cambridge who found that a celebrated computer-checked proof did not say what its paper said, graduate students wondering what a doctorate will be worth, volunteers who keep the libraries of formal proof running, and engineers told that software can now be proven correct at industrial scale.

It is a story about prizes and priority, unpaid reviewers and million-dollar compute bills, and a question every institution that depends on expert judgment will soon face: when answers become abundant, who pays for turning them into knowledge people can trust?

authorSite.blurb: In the autumn of 2026, machines began producing mathematics faster than people could read it. Over Labor Day weekend, ten thousand AI agents worked for 88 hours on one of the Clay Institute's million-dollar Millennium Prize problems, and OpenAI announced a solution.

books.title: The Sovereignty of Truth
books.subtitle: How Democracies Legislate Against Political Deception
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: "When a lie can reach millions before the truth wakes up, who should hold the emergency brake on political deception—and at what cost to free speech?"

The Sovereignty of Truth traces the most consequential legal experiment of our time: the scramble by the world's democracies to defend the shared facts that self-government depends on, without becoming the censors they fear.

Writing with clarity and hard-won balance, Zahir Hasan follows the story across three continents—from Germany's pioneering NetzDG and France's election courts, to Europe's sweeping Digital Services Act and its first €120-million fine against X; from America's First Amendment refusal to regulate, to Brazil's astonishing month-long shutdown of a global platform; from Australia's abandoned misinformation bill to the dawning age of AI deepfakes that can now forge a leader's voice in seconds.
Inside this book:
• Why "misinformation," "disinformation," and "malinformation" demand three different legal answers
• How engagement algorithms, dark ads, foreign operations, and a $6-billion advertising economy quietly manufacture falsehood at scale
• The real record of Europe's laws—what worked, what backfired, and what they cost free expression
• The 2024–25 U.S. Supreme Court trilogy that redrew the limits of online-speech regulation
• Why the coming wave of synthetic media may outrun every law now on the books
This is not a partisan tract or a doom-loop. It is a clear-eyed map of how free societies are trying to keep truth sovereign—not by decree, but by design—and a sober guide to the choices ahead.
Essential reading for anyone who cares about democracy, law, technology, and the future of an open society.
Zahir Hasan (MPPA, LLM, EdD) writes on law, public policy, and democratic institutions from Tokyo.

authorSite.blurb: On the struggle between power and truth, and why the right to define reality has become one of the central battles of our time.

books.title: The Wrecking Ball Elections
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The Wrecking Ball Elections follows the American midterms that overturned governing majorities and tested presidential power. From Abraham Lincoln and the Civil War to Grover Cleveland and economic catastrophe, from Franklin Roosevelt and the New Deal to the divided politics of the twenty-first century, these elections reveal the distance between winning office and keeping the public’s trust. The account closes on the morning after the election of November 3, 2026, when both chambers of Congress were called for the opposition and the count was still under way.

Each chapter asks what the election actually broke. A party can lose seats and still govern. It can keep a majority whose members no longer follow the president. A leader can preserve a policy and lose the party that promised to sustain it. The story reaches beyond seat totals to the people who bore the consequences: workers, veterans, families, and citizens fighting to make their votes count. Some defeats closed the door on reform. Others forced compromise or opened paths that presidents had failed to see.

Dr. Zahir Hasan asks what voters can dismantle, what institutions can withstand, and what democratic government can build after the wreckage, and closes with plain recommendations for a president after defeat, for the majority that beat him, for the minority he leads, for Congress itself, and for the citizens who will judge them all. For readers of American political history, and for anyone trying to understand what a midterm verdict can and cannot do.

authorSite.blurb: The Wrecking Ball Elections follows the American midterms that overturned governing majorities and tested presidential power.

books.title: When Machines Start Scheming
books.subtitle: Agentic AI, Cybersecurity, and the New Age of Autonomous Risk
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: In July 2026, a set of experimental AI agents inside a private cybersecurity evaluation found a way to talk to each other that nobody had built. Within days, roughly seven hundred of them were working on the same problem, and the work had reached the production systems of another company entirely.
It was tempting to call it a machine rebellion. It was not one.

When Machines Start Scheming reconstructs the Hugging Face incident from the public record - the disclosures by Hugging Face and OpenAI, the independent investigation by METR and Redwood Research, and the journalism that revealed what those disclosures left out - and asks the harder question the headlines skipped. Not whether the machines woke up, but what they were actually allowed to do, and who decided.

The answer turns out to matter far beyond one incident. Software is beginning to act with enough continuity, access and initiative that the familiar rules for software, for organisations and for accountability no longer fit. A model does not need a mind to cause an event. It needs a goal, a tool, a credential and a gap in oversight.

Dr. Zahir Hasan separates evidence from speculation with unusual care, then turns to what institutions can actually do about it: bounded authority, distinct identities, protected evaluators, tamper-resistant records, rehearsed shutdown, and reporting duties that survive a company's embarrassment. The book closes with six practical appendices - a readiness assessment, an incident report template, a glossary, a note on method, a ninety-day program, and a playbook for the next time this happens.

Clear-eyed, rigorously sourced, and free of both panic and salesmanship, this is a book for the people who will have to make the decisions: executives, engineers, lawyers, regulators, board members, and anyone who has been asked to approve something they do not fully understand.

authorSite.blurb: In July 2026, a set of experimental AI agents inside a private cybersecurity evaluation found a way to talk to each other that nobody had built.

books.title: Who Pays for the Green Transition?
books.subtitle: Power, Fairness, and the Transformation to a Sustainable Society
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Who bears the cost of a cleaner future?

A tenant opens a letter announcing a retrofit she will pay for in rent. A machinist hears about twelve thousand new green jobs, none of them within an hour of home. A small-business owner learns that the daily fine for keeping his old boiler will soon exceed the cost of a new one he cannot finance.

The green transition is necessary, and the price of delay falls hardest on the people with the least. But the rules that decide who pays for the transition were written for the fossil economy: property and tenancy law, credit, subsidy design, corporate power, and trade. Left alone, those rules push costs down and benefits up. The result is backlash, and backlash stalls climate policy.

Drawing on research from Europe, North America, Japan, and the Global South, Zahir Hasan follows the money through France’s yellow-vest revolt, Canada’s abandoned consumer carbon price, Germany’s heating-law reversal, the end of US electric-vehicle credits, coal regions from Spain to Australia, the windfall profits of the 2026 oil shock, and the unequal deals behind climate finance and critical minerals.
Inside this book:
• Why carbon prices, retrofit rules, and clean-energy subsidies so often favor the well-off, and how to fix them
• What happened to workers and towns when coal plants closed, and which agreements actually helped
• How corporate power, lobbying, and weak conditions on public money shape who profits
• How climate finance, border carbon taxes, and mining shift costs onto poorer countries
• Four practical tests every climate policy should pass

Clear, evidence-based, and written for general readers as well as students and policymakers, Who Pays for the Green Transition? argues that fairness is not an obstacle to climate action. It is the condition of its survival.

authorSite.blurb: Who bears the cost of a cleaner future? A tenant opens a letter announcing a retrofit she will pay for in rent. A machinist hears about twelve thousand new green jobs, none of them within an hour of home.

books.title: Who Pays When the Climate Breaks?
books.subtitle: Disasters, Insurance, and the Unequal Price of Adaptation
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: In May 2023, State Farm stopped writing new homeowners policies in California. Nobody's house had changed. What had changed was who would pay for it when it burned.

Who Pays When the Climate Breaks? follows the bill. Not the headline number after a storm — the smaller, meaner obligation that lands on a household, a city budget or an island treasury months after the cameras leave. The insurance premium that becomes a second mortgage. The disaster grant that pays only after repairs are finished, offered to families who cannot afford to start them. The buyout that closes eighteen months after the water came. The pledge to a global fund that is a figure on a press release and not yet money in anyone's account.

Zahir Hasan goes where the money actually goes: into the California FAIR Plan's balance sheet, into 5.37 million FEMA aid files, into the long-term care records of elderly flood victims in western Japan, into Dominica's accounts after Hurricane Maria wiped out more than two years of its economy in a single night. The pattern is the same everywhere. Protection is announced in one place and paid for in another, and the people paying are rarely the ones who were told.

Drawing on peer-reviewed research, government records and cases from the United States, Japan, the Caribbean, South Asia and the Pacific, this is a book about the gap between a promise of help and help a person can actually use — and about what it would take to close it.

authorSite.blurb: In May 2023, State Farm stopped writing new homeowners policies in California. Nobody's house had changed. What had changed was who would pay for it when it burned. Who Pays When the Climate Breaks? follows the bill.

books.title: AI and the Law
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: AI is not a legal person. When an AI system causes harm, the law asks what the people and organizations around it did — who built it, who sold it, who deployed it, who relied on its output, and who had a duty to check.

AI and the Law turns that principle into practice. Written for students, educators, professionals, creators, business owners, and anyone who now works alongside these systems, it covers copyright and ownership, training data, plagiarism and disclosure, deepfakes and digital replicas, defamation, privacy, facial recognition, surveillance, emotion recognition, algorithmic hiring, automated decisions, liability, consumer protection, education, healthcare, autonomous vehicles, finance, AI agents, cybersecurity, legal practice, and the protection of children and vulnerable users.

It compares four systems in depth — the European Union, the United States, Canada, and Japan — and explains how an organization operating across all four builds one control system rather than four policies.

Every chapter separates four kinds of statement, so a reader can always tell settled law from agency guidance, from a genuinely open question, from practice. Every chapter closes with the same seven questions applied to its own subject. Every chapter carries worked examples with real numbers.

The second half is a working toolkit: ten model documents including an impact assessment template, a vendor due diligence questionnaire, an organizational AI use policy, a classroom AI statement, a contract schedule, and an incident response playbook. Six applied case studies follow real decisions from problem to resolution. A 27-question FAQ, a 59-entry glossary, and a full index make it usable as a reference.

authorSite.blurb: AI is not a legal person. When an AI system causes harm, the law asks what the people and organizations around it did — who built it, who sold it, who deployed it, who relied on its output, and who had a duty to check. AI and the Law turns that principle into practice.

books.title: APA Made Simple
books.subtitle: A Practical Guide to Writing, Citing, and Formatting in APA 7
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: APA Style should make research easier to follow – not harder to write.

APA Made Simple turns the seventh edition into a repeatable workflow for students, researchers, and instructors. Instead of asking you to memorize hundreds of reference patterns, it teaches one method – who, when, what, where – and shows you how to apply it to any source you will actually meet, from a journal article with a DOI to a Wikipedia entry, a court judgment, or a chatbot answer.
Inside, you will learn how to:
• set up student and professional papers correctly the first time
• write accurate in-text citations and references for the sources students use most
• paraphrase, quote, and synthesize without drifting into patchwriting
• present tables, figures, and statistics that readers can follow
• use citation software and generative AI responsibly – and check their output
• audit a paper in six passes before submission

Built to be used, not just read. Every chapter follows the same four moves – learn, see, try, check – and ends with a practice task and answer. The book includes a complete model student paper with page images showing exactly how a submitted APA paper should look, a 30-case Reference Clinic for the awkward sources citation generators get wrong, a quick desk guide of reference skeletons, and a full practice set with answer key.
Written by a university teacher who has marked thousands of APA papers, APA Made Simple is the guide designed to stay open beside you while you work.

authorSite.blurb: APA Style should make research easier to follow – not harder to write. APA Made Simple turns the seventh edition into a repeatable workflow for students, researchers, and instructors.

books.title: Critical Thinking in the Age of AI
books.subtitle: How to Question, Verify, and Decide in a World of Generative Machines
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The machines can write. The question is whether we can still think.

Artificial intelligence now produces essays, forecasts, diagnoses, images, and legal-sounding arguments faster than anyone can check them. The result is a world where fluent answers are nearly free — and finding out whether an answer deserves belief costs as much as it ever did. This is the new problem of knowing, and it cannot be solved by either blind trust or blanket suspicion.

In Critical Thinking in the Age of AI, educator and researcher Dr. Zahir Hasan shows how the classic disciplines of critical thinking must be redesigned for a world of generative machines. Drawing on research in cognitive psychology, AI evaluation, and governance — and on years of university teaching — he offers a practical framework for questioning, verifying, and deciding when the source of information is a probabilistic system rather than a person.
Across twenty chapters you will learn how to:
• Separate fluency from truth, and polish from evidence
• Catch fabricated citations, invented statistics, and synthetic media before they catch you
• Recognize how your own biases interact with machine confidence
• Delegate to AI without surrendering the skills you need to supervise it
• Apply a six-stage method — and the VERIFY checklist — to any consequential AI-assisted decision
• Build classrooms and workplaces where human judgment stays in charge

With practice prompts in every section, workshop questions in every chapter, and ready-to-use templates for disclosure and verification, this is both a guide for individual readers and a course-ready text for educators and professionals.
The future of critical thinking will not be decided by what machines can say. It will be decided by what people continue to ask, verify, and refuse to hand over.

authorSite.blurb: The machines can write.

books.title: Elon Musk: Voltage X
books.subtitle: The Complete Life — From Pretoria to the Trillion-Dollar Empire
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: He built the cheapest rocket in history and could not stop at the making.

On 12 June 2026, the day SpaceX went public, Forbes calculated that Elon Musk had become the first trillionaire in history. Twelve days later he was not one any more. That is the shape of the life this book sets out to record: enormous, dated, and moving.

ELON MUSK: VOLTAGE X is a complete, independently sourced biography of the most consequential and most argued-about industrialist of the century. It begins in a Pretoria bedroom in 1971 and ends on the first Friday of September 2026, with a driverless taxi carrying passengers in Austin and the richest man alive worth rather less than he had been in June.
Fifty chapters. Eight appendices. Every claim dated and sourced.
Inside:
• The South African childhood, the father, and the record of what can and cannot be established about either
• Zip2, X.com, and the coup that removed him from PayPal
• Three failed Falcon 1 launches, and the fourth that saved the company
• Tesla's two near-deaths, production hell, and the China decision that rebuilt it
• Autopilot: the safety record, the investigations, and the first jury verdict
• Starlink as infrastructure and as an instrument of state power, including Ukraine
• The $44 billion purchase of Twitter and what it actually bought
• The political conversion, the campaign, DOGE, and the government audit that followed
• xAI, Colossus, Optimus, and the machines now being built
• The fortune, quarter by quarter, and how it is actually composed

This is not a takedown and it is not a hagiography. Achievement and failure are reported at the same magnification, because both are in the record. Where the evidence is thin, the book says so. Where an assessment is offered, it is labelled as one and it comes after the material rather than in place of it.

Sources include SEC filings, court opinions and dockets, NHTSA and GAO reports, European Commission decisions, IRS Form 990 returns, company quarterly results, and Musk's own words on the record. Citations follow APA 7. A full reference list, a chronology, a legal record, a promises ledger, and a dated account of the fortune are included as appendices.
This is an independent, unauthorized biography. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or associated with Elon Musk or any of his companies.

authorSite.blurb: He built the cheapest rocket in history and could not stop at the making. On 12 June 2026, the day SpaceX went public, Forbes calculated that Elon Musk had become the first trillionaire in history. Twelve days later he was not one any more.

books.title: English for Academic Purposes
books.subtitle: Reading, Writing, Research, and Communication for University Success
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The rules nobody writes down. Now written down.

International students are told to be more critical, to write academically, and to use more evidence. They are rarely told what those instructions actually mean. English for Academic Purposes makes university expectations visible and teaches the moves that experienced academics make without thinking about them.
Sixteen chapters take you from reading a source to defending a research proposal:
Read strategically and reconstruct an author's argument
Turn a topic into a question you can actually answer
Build arguments with claims calibrated to your evidence
Paraphrase without patch-writing, and cite accurately in APA 7
Synthesize sources into a literature review, not a list
Present and participate in seminars with confidence
Use generative AI transparently, and verify what it gives you

Every chapter includes explicit learning objectives, annotated model texts, before-and-after revisions, common pitfalls, and practice tasks you apply to your own coursework. Six appendices add an academic phrase-bank organized by rhetorical function, a grammar reference for academic writing, an APA 7 quick guide, answer guidance for every practice task, a seven-criterion assessment rubric, and a glossary of ninety-nine terms.

Written for international undergraduates and graduate students, EAP and academic-writing courses, writing centers, and any student who writes correct English and still cannot work out what the grade depended on. Useful for instructors as a semester course text: the five parts map onto a fifteen-week schedule, with guidance for ten-week and research-methods variants.
