books.title: GRIT Unplugged
books.subtitle: The Unfiltered Truth About Getting Back Up
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Every setback comes with a story attached about what it means. Most of those stories are wrong.

Dr. Zahir Hasan was denied a graduate degree he had already earned — no clear explanation, no real path to appeal, just a closed door. It could have been the end of the story. Instead, it became the starting point for a career that eventually included a Master of Laws, a doctorate in education, and a life spent teaching university students how to face their own versions of the same fall.

GRIT Unplugged: The Unfiltered Truth About Getting Back Up is not a book about turning your worst moment into a hidden gift, and it does not promise that resilience will feel inspiring while it's happening. Drawing on decades of resilience research — Bandura, Bonanno, Seligman, and others — alongside his own uneven, sometimes unglamorous path back up, Hasan makes the case that getting back up is not a personality trait. It is a skill, built through ordinary practice, available to anyone willing to start again.

Written in a warm, story-driven voice rather than a textbook one, each chapter pairs real research with a real moment from the author's life — moving across four countries, a denied degree, and a slow rebuild — to leave readers with something more useful than motivation: a practical, honest way to get back up, again and again, for as long as it takes.
For anyone who has been knocked down and suspects the usual comeback story is missing something.

authorSite.blurb: Every setback comes with a story attached about what it means.

books.title: Law for Everyday Life
books.subtitle: A Practical Guide to Contracts, Employment, Privacy, Consumer Rights, and the Internet
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The lease on the table. The job you can leave. The charge that will not cancel. The post that will not come down. Ordinary life runs on rules most people never see until something goes wrong.

Law for Everyday Life explains, in plain language, how those rules actually work: contracts and the fine print behind every click, wages and overtime, security deposits and evictions, refunds and chargebacks, personal data, online defamation, copyright in the age of AI, and what really happens when you sue someone or get sued yourself. Each chapter ends with a worked example showing how a real dispute plays out, and the appendices supply the tools: document checklists, sample letters you can adapt, a glossary, quick answers to common questions, and a one-hour annual legal health check.

Written for people who live inside contracts, not courtrooms, this book teaches the habit that wins disputes: know the rule, know the deadline, and keep the paper. It is a practical guide, not legal advice, with comparative notes on Japan for readers whose lives cross borders.

authorSite.blurb: The lease on the table.

books.title: Power Beyond Position
books.subtitle: Workplace Harassment, Informal Authority, and Corporate Accountability in Japan
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A retired senior employee returns under a new reporting line. The organization chart says one thing; longstanding connections, expertise and informal loyalty say another. Who actually holds power, and when does resistance become impossible?

Japanese law has an answer, and it is more capable than most managers realize: workplace superiority is assessed functionally, not by job title. A person with no managerial rank at all can hold it, and the courts have said so.

But the law's machinery runs on complaints, and the complaints mostly never come. In the most recent national survey, fewer than one worker in twenty who experienced power harassment used the consultation desk every employer in Japan is legally required to provide. Two-thirds of those who stayed silent said nothing would be solved whatever they did. Where employers did know, more than half did nothing in particular.

Power Beyond Position sets out the statutory framework, works through the decided Japanese cases, and confronts that reporting gap directly. It argues that Japanese employers have bought compliance without buying protection, and it shows what closing the gap would actually require of employers, boards, policymakers and managers.
Inside:
The three-element legal test and the six official categories, anchored in real decided cases
Why informal authority escapes supervision, and how to diagnose it
The re-employed returner: the situation that prompted the book
A dedicated chapter on the reporting gap, built on government survey and compensation data
A table of Japanese cases, a role charter, a model policy, a complaint-intake record and an investigation protocol
Written for managers, HR and compliance professionals, employment-law students, worker advocates, expatriate professionals in Japan, and readers interested in Japanese corporate governance.

authorSite.blurb: A retired senior employee returns under a new reporting line.

books.title: Project-Based Learning in Action
books.subtitle: A Practical Guide to Designing, Teaching, Assessing, and Sustaining Meaningful Learning
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Project-based learning can produce deep, memorable learning—or weeks of busy activity. The difference is design.

Project-Based Learning in Action is a practical field guide for K-12 teachers, instructional coaches, and school leaders who want projects that protect rigor while expanding student agency. Using the BUILD cycle, Zahir Hasan shows how to begin with worthy learning, frame authentic problems, guide inquiry, teach collaboration, use critique and revision, assess individual understanding, and recover when projects drift.
Inside this book you will find:
Twenty-three chapters on designing, teaching, assessing, and sustaining high-quality PBL
Six complete project models across grade bands and subjects
Twenty adaptable project starters
Planning templates, rubrics, family communication samples, and a day-by-day first project
An honest reading of the research, equity from the first week, and AI treated as a useful assistant—not a substitute
This is not a collection of project ideas. It is a working system for making knowledge usable.

authorSite.blurb: Project-based learning can produce deep, memorable learning—or weeks of busy activity.

books.title: Raising a Multilingual Child
books.subtitle: A Practical, Research-Based Family Plan for Ages 2–14
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Your child can keep your languages. Here is the plan.

Most advice about raising bilingual or multilingual children stops at the method: one parent, one language; minority language at home; "just be consistent." Then real life arrives. School takes over. One parent works late. The child understands everything and answers in the wrong language. This book starts where that advice ends.

Raising a Multilingual Child is a working system for families with children aged 2 to 14, built on verified research and shown in full through two families you follow from their first planning conversation to a review ninety days later: the Okada-Frasers in Tokyo, protecting English against Japanese school, and the Mensah-Lindqvists in Copenhagen, bringing Twi back for a nine-year-old who loves football and a twelve-year-old who has started to refuse it.
Inside you will find:
• A seven-day language audit and the TIES test, shown completed for a real week
• Five family language strategies, with each family's written strategy and exceptions
• Age-specific chapters for 2–4, 5–7, 8–10, and 11–14, with a four-week launch plan, a six-week project, and a reset meeting with a resisting teenager
• Filled-in scripts and letters: a call plan for grandparents, a note to a teacher, a brief for a babysitter, a communication profile for a speech-language pathologist
• Practical answers to mixing, reluctance, inconsistency, sibling influence, teasing, literacy in two writing systems, and developmental concerns
• A complete 90-day family plan with dates, the day-90 review as a conversation, and every worksheet shown filled in before the blank
• Sixty activities, six of them worked out in full
• Fifty-three verified research sources, explained in plain language.
Written by an educator and parent-facing researcher based in Tokyo, this is a book to use on a Tuesday evening—not a book merely to admire.

authorSite.blurb: Your child can keep your languages. Here is the plan. Most advice about raising bilingual or multilingual children stops at the method: one parent, one language; minority language at home; "just be consistent." Then real life arrives. School takes over. One parent works late.

books.title: Raising Screen-Smart Kids
books.subtitle: A Practical Parent’s Guide to Healthy Digital Habits from Ages 2 to 12
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Your child is not addicted. Your home is unplanned. Here is the plan.

It is 7:18 on a school morning and the tablet has been asked to go away three times. If that scene is familiar, this book is for you. It does not tell you to ban screens, and it does not tell you to give up. It shows you how to build a family system in which technology has useful jobs, clear boundaries, and no automatic right to displace sleep, play, paper, and conversation.

Drawing on the current guidance of pediatric bodies in North America, Europe, Australia, and Japan, and on the research behind it, Raising Screen-Smart Kids gives parents of children aged two to twelve a seven-step method called BALANCE, a fourteen-day family reset, and a toolkit they can use tonight:
• 74 alternatives that meet the need a screen was meeting
• 50 word-for-word scripts for the hardest moments: “just one more,” “everyone else has it,” the meltdown, the sneaked device
• 30 family case files, 20 troubleshooting cards, and answers to the 25 questions parents ask most
• 12 printable worksheets, each shown blank and then filled in by one family

• a step-by-step walkthrough of the parental controls on iPhone and iPad, Android, Nintendo Switch, PlayStation, Xbox, YouTube Kids, Netflix, Roblox, and the home router, and the eight ways children get around them
• one family’s complete fourteen-day reset, setbacks included
• an appendix comparing official screen-time guidance in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, Japan, and from the World Health Organization

Age-by-age chapters cover the toddler and preschool years, ages six to nine, and ages ten to twelve, including the first-phone decision, gaming, group chats, and why public social media can wait. A chapter on paper, pencil, and books explains what the research actually shows about reading and handwriting on screens, and what to protect.
Practical, evidence-based, and free of guilt. The target is not zero screens. It is a childhood with technology in its place.

authorSite.blurb: Your child is not addicted. Your home is unplanned. Here is the plan. It is 7:18 on a school morning and the tablet has been asked to go away three times. If that scene is familiar, this book is for you. It does not tell you to ban screens, and it does not tell you to give up.

books.title: Take Back Your Hours
books.subtitle: Simple Ways to Manage Your Time in a Distracted World
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Where does your day actually go?

The average person now spends three to five hours a day on a phone — more than forty full days a year — and most of it vanishes without leaving anything behind. You are not lazy, and you are not broken. You are living in the most distracting environment in human history, and nobody handed you a manual for it.

This is the manual. In twenty short chapters, each ending with one simple thing to try today, you will learn how to find the hours you didn’t know you had: silence the notifications that interrupt you dozens of times a day, choose the one thing that makes each day count, tame the endless feeds, protect your evenings and the people you love — and restart gently when it all falls apart, as it sometimes will.

No apps to buy. No complicated system. Just simple, human-sized changes, backed by real research and drawn from years of teaching in classrooms on three continents. Follow three relatable companions — a manager drowning in email, a nurse with two young children, and a graduate student whose evenings kept disappearing — as they take their hours back. Then take back yours.

authorSite.blurb: Where does your day actually go?

books.title: The AI Classroom
books.subtitle: A Practical Handbook for Teachers and Administrators: Assessment Redesign, Academic Integrity, Policy and Governance
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Most books about AI in education tell you what to think. This one tells you what to do on Monday.

Three years after generative AI arrived in classrooms, roughly nine in ten students use it for assessed work and roughly two in ten teachers work somewhere that has told them the rules. The AI Classroom closes that gap.

Written by a university teacher with degrees in law, public policy and education, it reports what the research actually shows, separates legal obligation from good intention across six jurisdictions, and then hands over the documents. Nothing here is a blank template with brackets in it.
What is inside
The two-lane method — secure the few assessments that matter across a programme, and design the rest openly
Detection, honestly — what the tools do, what they cannot do, why they misfire on second-language writers, and the arithmetic that settles the decision for your institution
A fair-process framework for academic integrity that survives an ombudsman's review, with the burden of proof where it belongs
Two complete model policies, one for schools and one for universities, annotated with the reasoning behind every clause
Six worked assessment conversions, before and after, from primary to postgraduate
Three integrity case files with every document produced, including the case the institution got wrong and had to remedy
Eleven annotated letters, including the reply to a parent demanding that you use detection software
A vendor questionnaire, scorecard and twelve-clause contract library, plus a worked data protection impact assessment
Ten complete lesson plans and a scripted two-hour staff session
Four case studies carried end to end, with the documents

Current to August 2026, including the changes most guidance has not caught up with: the deferral of the EU AI Act's high-risk obligations for education to December 2027, the extension of the US web accessibility deadlines, and the retraction of the most-cited meta-analysis in the field.

Over 320 pages. Written for heads of department, deputy heads, provosts, teaching and learning leads, integrity officers, and any teacher who has been asked to hold a line the institution has not drawn.

authorSite.blurb: Most books about AI in education tell you what to think.

books.title: The Gap in the Middle
books.subtitle: The Linguistic Wars, the Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis, and the Architecture of Human Thought
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: In 2007, researchers sat Russian and English speakers in front of three blue squares and asked them to point at the odd one out. The Russians were faster by about the time it takes to blink, twice. That sliver of time has since been asked to prove that language decides what the world looks like to us.
The Gap in the Middle is about the distance between what an experiment showed and what the headline said it showed.

Dr. Zahir Hasan works through the evidence on colour, space, time, number, memory, bilingualism and the brain, and follows the argument into classrooms, institutions, translation and artificial intelligence. Along the way: a fire inspector who noticed that the word "empty" on a petrol drum had organised somebody's attention badly; the researcher who published the universalist result in 1969 and the relativist one in 1984, with good evidence both times; three men whose grammar had been destroyed and who could still do nested arithmetic; and a bilingual advantage that dissolved under 891 effect sizes.

The book's proposal is a framework of conditional influence: name the linguistic resource, name the cognitive operation, state the conditions, and say how far the conclusion travels. It is a careful account of how language can matter without becoming a prison for the mind.

authorSite.blurb: In 2007, researchers sat Russian and English speakers in front of three blue squares and asked them to point at the odd one out. The Russians were faster by about the time it takes to blink, twice.

books.title: University Students and Artificial Intelligence
books.subtitle: Adoption, Learning, Integrity, and Governance in Japan, the United States, and Europe
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Ninety-five per cent of UK undergraduates now use artificial intelligence. In Japan the figure reached ninety-two per cent in two years. Almost no university has caught up.

University Students and Artificial Intelligence is a comparative, mixed-methods study of what students actually do with generative AI in Japan, the United States, and Europe — and what their institutions are doing about it. Drawing on twenty national and international student surveys, seven meta-analyses, randomised experimental evidence, freedom-of-information data on academic misconduct, and the EU Artificial Intelligence Act, it moves past the exhausted argument about cheating to the harder questions of learning value, authorship, equity, and institutional legitimacy.

The book answers questions most commentary avoids. Does AI use actually improve learning? (The evidence is weaker than almost everyone citing it realises — and the field’s most-quoted study was retracted.) Can detection software support a misconduct finding? (It produced a sixty-one per cent false positive rate against writers who learned English as a second language.) What does the EU AI Act really require of universities? (Far less, and far more specifically, than the commentary suggests.)

Every statistic is reported with its population, sample size, and fieldwork period, and was checked against the organisation that published it. Widely circulated figures that failed that check are named. Two appendices give readers the entire evidence base in one table and an eight-question protocol for judging new statistics as they appear.

The result is a practical, evidence-led framework — CLEAR — for university leaders, faculty, academic-integrity officers, education policymakers, and graduate students in education, law, and public policy.
Zahir Hasan, MPPA, LLM, EdD, teaches at a university in Tokyo and writes on public policy, law, education, and institutional governance.

authorSite.blurb: Adoption, Learning, Integrity, and Governance in Japan, the United States, and Europe. A comparative study of what students actually do with generative AI — and what their universities are doing about it.

books.title: Warren Buffett
books.subtitle: From Omaha Beginnings to Berkshire Hathaway—and the Discipline of Long-Term Wealth
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Warren Buffett is often reduced to a handful of slogans about patience and value. His real achievement was more demanding: he built an institution in which patient judgment could operate at extraordinary scale.

From Depression-era Omaha and teenage business ventures to Benjamin Graham’s classroom, the Buffett partnerships, and the transformation of a failing textile mill into Berkshire Hathaway, this biography follows the full arc of Buffett’s life and work. It explains how insurance float, permanent capital, decentralized management, disciplined acquisitions, and an earned reputation became mutually reinforcing advantages.

The successes are examined alongside the errors—Berkshire textiles, Dexter Shoe, General Re, Kraft Heinz, Precision Castparts, and delayed responses to change. The book also confronts governance, labor oversight, philanthropy, family cost, and the challenge of making a founder-shaped culture durable.

Current through Buffett’s move to chairman emeritus on September 18, 2026, this is both a life story and a clear analytical guide to the ideas, structures, and trade-offs behind one of the most consequential business records in modern history.

authorSite.blurb: Warren Buffett is often reduced to a handful of slogans about patience and value. His real achievement was more demanding: he built an institution in which patient judgment could operate at extraordinary scale.

books.title: A Court of Knives
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The empress is dead. The will named two heirs. The knives choose neither.

Restored to a name twenty years erased, Lucan Corvinus is now the most wanted man in the empire — accused of murdering the woman he tried to save. With Sigrun Halvard beside him he rides for the top of the world to find the one living witness who can prove who destroyed his father, while the Order's quiet men ride the same road ahead of them.

Behind him, a ghost ship sails into harbour with her crew standing dead at their stations. In the capital, an old man with a black bee on his cuff teaches a new emperor how to lose an empire. And beyond the edge of the maps, the cold that stopped that crew comes south, eight miles a day, patient as arithmetic.
The court has knives. The north has winter. And something out in the white has learned to wear a dead man's face.
Book Two of the Draconate Saga — epic fantasy of dragons, morally gray houses, and a slow-burning love story between two people who both expect to die young. Best read after A Throne of Cinders.

authorSite.blurb: The empress is dead.

books.title: A Reply in Plasma
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Seventeen years after the Sun answered humanity's first bounded test, the plasma ring beyond Mars contracts early. Palinode, the station built to study it, lies inside a changing field that can carry fragments of an interstellar archive. The incoming records suggest thousands of worlds—and expose a failed node seeking somewhere to place its load. When a stolen coil leaves the station and Jonah Vale substitutes an unauthorized maintenance state for a far more dangerous pulse, the immediate crisis is contained but the consequence begins traveling outward at light speed. Anika Rao, Leila Sen, Elise Varga, and Emi Hayashi must create public rules for a system no one owns, while engineers design receivers whose most important feature is the ability to forget. A Reply in Plasma is Book Two of The Long Meridian, a hard-science-fiction novel about low-bandwidth contact, distributed custody, and the difference between technical competence and legitimate authority.

authorSite.blurb: Seventeen years after the Sun answered humanity's first bounded test, the plasma ring beyond Mars contracts early. Palinode, the station built to study it, lies inside a changing field that can carry fragments of an interstellar archive.

books.title: A Throne of Cinders
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Nine dragons are left in the world, and every one of them is a throne.

Lucan has spent his life on a mountain, stitching up what dragonlords do to each other. He knows what the gift costs. He has buried its price. Then a dying rider is carried up to the sanctum whispering a name Lucan has never heard: his own.

Dragged to the golden capital of an empire circling a dying empress's crown, the son of an executed traitor becomes the piece every player wants — the Order, the princes, the spymaster, the throne itself. There is one door out of the trap. It is guarded by the only dragon no one has ever ridden and lived.
And far to the north, past the edge of the maps, something older than the empire has begun to feed.

A Throne of Cinders opens the Draconate Saga: an epic fantasy of dragons, morally gray houses, and a world that ended once before — for readers who like their politics sharp, their dragons dangerous, and their heroes earned. Book One of ten.

authorSite.blurb: Nine dragons are left in the world, and every one of them is a throne.

books.title: Brand of Gold
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: She stole a dragon's soul. Now it will not let her go.

Rook Ithara owes the Pale Ledger three lives, and the Ledger does not recalculate. So when a fence offers her a seal that can clear a life-account, she takes the job. One relic. One night. Out before the third bell.

The relic is a Heartscale, and it brands her — to a dying black wyrm with silver wire in her throat, and to the last unbound rider alive. A man Rook has never met, who wants her gone by morning and needs her breathing by dark. Two souls can hold a dragon. Three can command a flight. The brand lasts until one of the bound three dies.

Beneath the city of Vesperhold, twenty-six dragons wait in stalls of black iron, clipped and branded and milked for heat. High Warden Orsel wants a third soul on the binding, and with it every wyrm in the empire on one chain. He is courteous about it. He is patient. He is not wrong about the arithmetic — the pipes run warm because the animals are chained, and eleven thousand people sleep over that nave.
Rook does not work for free. She does not kneel. And the only thing standing between a city and a leash is a thief who has never been able to stop counting.

Book One of the Scale and Sorrow trilogy. A dark fantasy romance with a forced soul-bond, a morally grey antagonist who argues in good faith, and a dragon who is nobody's mount. Explicit content. For readers 18+.

authorSite.blurb: She stole a dragon's soul. Now it will not let her go. Rook Ithara owes the Pale Ledger three lives, and the Ledger does not recalculate. So when a fence offers her a seal that can clear a life-account, she takes the job. One relic. One night. Out before the third bell.

books.title: The Arctic Signal
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The first conspiracy was hidden in data. The second is buried beneath the ice.

Eighteen months after the Singapore crisis, an encrypted knock travels through an undersea cable beneath Greenland’s ice. The technician who hears it vanishes, and the same governments that buried the Meridian Protocol begin preparing for a war their own systems may be inventing.

Hana Malik, Daniel Mercer, and Aiko Tanabe are drawn back together as a new platform called Atlas converts disputed signals into automatic authority. From Copenhagen and Nuuk to Islamabad, Washington, and a cable ship in the North Atlantic, they race to find the physical record before a fifteen-minute countdown makes suspicion irreversible. This time, exposing the lie may be as dangerous as letting the world believe it.
Book Two of The Copenhagen Protocol. Can be read on its own, but starts best after The Singapore Cipher.

authorSite.blurb: The first conspiracy was hidden in data. The second is buried beneath the ice. Eighteen months after the Singapore crisis, an encrypted knock travels through an undersea cable beneath Greenland’s ice.

books.title: The Ashen Veil Saga
books.subtitle: The Commonborn
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Three hundred years ago, twenty-four people talked a mountain range into standing up. It cost each of them a memory, and the stone chose which one.

At a quarter past four on a winter morning, the wind over Kest stops. Not drops — stops. Fires burn without giving heat. Breath stops showing. And the iron coming down out of the northern hills is the wrong iron: it is not for making things, it is for taking the permission out of them.

Silas of Lowford is a village smith who can hear what stone remembers. His younger brother Jonah can feel a storm before it has decided to be one. Neither of them is any use in a rank of soldiers — which is precisely the argument Silas makes when the fort at Northwatch, eleven hundred people and a captain who has never once failed to send a return, goes nineteen days in silence, and the Reeve of Kest sits weighing whether to send five hundred men or nobody at all.
Send two, Silas tells him. Give us four days and a mule.

What waits in the north is the thing their ancestors buried and mistook for a finished job. And behind them, in a city that keeps flawless accounts of everything except itself, a ledger-keeper named Vaskell Ordan has been quietly leaning on Kest for years — and the stone has been the only thing keeping count.
The warning is carved over the gate of the White City, worn smooth by generations who recited it at midwinter without ever knowing it was a set of instructions:
Let no child go north unless his hands know stone and his lungs know sky.
Book One of The Ashen Veil Saga. Includes a map of Vyr Kallan, the White City.

authorSite.blurb: Three hundred years ago, twenty-four people talked a mountain range into standing up.

books.title: The Bilbao Sequence
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Humanity has learned how to turn back the clock. It may not survive the second chance.

At 5:17 on a rain-dark morning in Bilbao, systems analyst Zam Malik finds his oldest friend dying beneath La Salve Bridge — a man of forty-seven who has aged nearly a century overnight. The impossible death points to a hidden breakthrough: a treatment that can return an adult body to youth. Billionaire Elias Vale financed the research, but his ambition reaches far beyond immortality. He is building a ship for Nysa, a world twelve light-years away, and he intends to decide who lives long enough to reach it.

As rejuvenation escapes the laboratory, nations fracture, black markets spread, births become political weapons, and millions discover that eternal youth comes with a thirty-day leash. To free them, Zam and the physician Leire Etxebarria must turn a cure into something no corporation or government can own — while Vale engineers the catastrophe that will make leaving Earth seem like humanity’s only choice.
The Bilbao Sequence is Book One of The Age Beyond Earth, a near-future science fiction series that begins with a real 2026 clinical result and asks what a longer life would cost.

authorSite.blurb: Humanity has learned how to turn back the clock. It may not survive the second chance. At 5:17 on a rain-dark morning in Bilbao, systems analyst Zam Malik finds his oldest friend dying beneath La Salve Bridge — a man of forty-seven who has aged nearly a century overnight.

books.title: The Chronicles of Aethelgard
books.subtitle: The Whispering Woods
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Zach doesn't want to move into a crumbling old house in the middle of nowhere. Then his little sister Raana finds a glowing key hidden inside a dusty trunk in the attic — and everything changes.

The key opens a tunnel of living roots that drops the two siblings straight into Aethelgard: a world of floating islands, singing crystals, and a very opinionated badger named Barnaby, who insists they've arrived exactly when they were needed.

Because Aethelgard is running out of light. A silent grey fog called the Silencing is swallowing color, sound, and warmth wherever it spreads, and the ancient Aetherstones that power the whole realm are going dark, one by one. Only two children from beyond the roots — the Echo-Children of old legend — can stop it.

Zach sees the world as a puzzle: patterns, sequences, symbols waiting to be solved. Raana sees it as something to trust: a giant crystal beast, a bridge that only responds to sound, a home worth saving. Together they'll have to cross the Bridge of Whispers, outrun the Shadow-Stalkers, and reach the long-sealed Great Aether-Pool before the last light goes out for good.
It's only the first Aetherstone. Six more are waiting.
A gently spooky, richly illustrated fantasy adventure for readers ages 7–10 who love puzzles, magical creatures, and siblings who make a surprisingly great team.

authorSite.blurb: Zach doesn't want to move into a crumbling old house in the middle of nowhere.

books.title: The Custodian
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: On one Earth it misses. On the other it does not.

A rock one point four kilometres across will cross the Earth's orbit on the eleventh of March, 2074. Three years of patient observation settle where it goes. On Daniel Mercer's Earth it passes at forty-one thousand kilometres. On Mara's it does not pass at all.

Two sealed worlds have four years, a heavy-lift industry built for a machine nobody wants back, and a line that carries speech and nothing else. So a spacecraft is built by dictation: a father reading numbers to his daughter across a wall, forty minutes at a time, with both worlds listening.

And at the centre of eight thousand histories a woman with Mara's face, who can see every sky at once, is learning what an occupied origin does to the worlds around it. Every line that hears her acts alike. Lines that act alike become one line. The thing the network was built to prevent is her.

The Custodian completes The Other Earth Trilogy: a novel about difference, what it is worth, and what two Earths give up so that they can go on being two. Written in the classic tradition of hard science fiction, with the science explained and the wonder left to the reader.

authorSite.blurb: On one Earth it misses. On the other it does not. A rock one point four kilometres across will cross the Earth's orbit on the eleventh of March, 2074. Three years of patient observation settle where it goes. On Daniel Mercer's Earth it passes at forty-one thousand kilometres.

books.title: The Elk Kingdom
books.subtitle: Book I: The Silent Veil
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Long before the first elf learned to speak, the Great Elk and the First Elf made a silent pact under the oldest tree in the world: the elk would carry the living songs of the forest in their antlers, and the elves would listen and keep the quiet places safe.
Every few seasons, the songs fade into a deep hush called the Silent Veil — and the Great Elk chooses a new Listener, almost always a child whose heart is still open.
This year, the Veil has come three seasons too early.

Six-year-old Elian has always heard more than most. When the ancient carving on his bedroom wall flickers dark, he knows the pact is breaking. Drawn alone into the mist, he meets the Great Elk face to face — and senses a second shadow moving just behind it, one that leaves no tracks at all.
As the forest's songs grow fainter and his family searches through the night for answers, Elian must decide whether to step into the silence and answer a call that could save everything he loves.

The Elk Kingdom, Book I: The Silent Veil is a gently spooky, richly illustrated read-aloud adventure about family, courage, and the magic of really listening — perfect for children ages 6-9 who love enchanted forests and stories with heart.
Book 1 of The Elk Kingdom series. Book II: The Hollow Heart is coming soon.

authorSite.blurb: Six-year-old Elian has always heard more than most. When the ancient pact between the Great Elk and the First Elf begins to break early, he must decide whether to answer a call that could save everything he loves.

books.title: The Exile’s Blood
books.subtitle: A Dark Fantasy Novel
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The king is dying.
The bloodline is hunted.
And the mountain is waking.

In a remote northern village, eighteen-year-old Aidan lives a quiet life with his father—a teacher of forbidden arts—and his mother. When soldiers come for his father, the truth of an ancient royal bloodline is revealed. Hunted across frozen forests and into the shadow of an ancient dragon, Aidan must decide how much of himself he is willing to burn to save what remains of his family—and what the mountain will demand in return.

Shadowfire is not a gift. It is a debt. Every use of the cold black-red flame exacts a price in memory, years, or pieces of the soul. As Aidan learns the true cost of the power in his blood, he is drawn into a deadly struggle for the throne, the awakening of the Ashen Wyrm, and a dangerous romance that may either save him or destroy him.
The Exile’s Blood is the first book in The Shadowfire Throne, a dark fantasy trilogy of forbidden magic, dragons, political intrigue, and the heavy price of power.

authorSite.blurb: The king is dying.

books.title: The First Shadow
books.subtitle: The Whispering Realms - Episode 1
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: In the ancient elven realm of Elen’dor, peace has lasted for centuries. The trees still sing. The stars still shine.
But young Aelira has begun to notice something others refuse to see.
A single black leaf. A silence where birds should sing. A presence in the mist that watches and waits.
When Aelira discovers a shadow that should not exist, she learns a terrible truth: something sealed long ago is beginning to wake.
And for the first time, it has noticed her.
The First Shadow is the opening episode in The Whispering Realms, a mysterious and atmospheric fantasy series for readers ages 8–10.

authorSite.blurb: The opening story of The Whispering Realms. Young Aelira discovers that some shadows carry messages — and some messages change everything.

books.title: The High Tower of Glass
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: When her sister Greta returns from the forest border with empty eyes and a hollow chest, Clara knows the old stories are true — and that they always ask for payment.

She catches Greta's vanishing voice in a silk handkerchief and steps past the moss line into the Black Ridge Wood, where fairy-tale logic is law and every gift has a price. Guided only by a crust of wine-soaked bread, an unblessed iron nail, and the warnings of the border-spirits she meets along the way, Clara crosses the Great Bog to bargain with the Lord of the Hollow Glass himself.

To unlock his mirrored palace and win back her sister's voice, Clara will have to give up something of her own — the shadow of her left arm — and unravel a three-hundred-year-old secret sealed inside a vanishing carpenter's watch.

A dark, atmospheric fairy tale for readers of Neil Gaiman and Susanna Clarke, The High Tower of Glass is a short story of about 9,000 words that opens Book 1 of The Hollow Glass Series. Book 2, The Hall of Salt and Bone, follows.

authorSite.blurb: When her sister Greta returns from the forest border with empty eyes and a hollow chest, Clara knows the old stories are true — and that they always ask for payment.

books.title: The House Beneath the Ash
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A city built on stolen names. A house that remembers every lie.
In the riverbound city of Veyr, law is written in ledgers, sealed with memory, and enforced by the Lantern Court — an institution that turns children into paperwork and grief into currency.
When Mara Venn hears her supposedly dead mother's voice inside a forbidden ember, she follows it into the House Beneath the Ash, a buried labyrinth of lanterns, winter camps, and erased identities.

As Mara descends with a skeptical fisher, a guilty memory-finder, and a raven tied to a lost girl's past, she uncovers the Court's oldest crime: an oath that once promised "no child will be abandoned to the cold," quietly rewritten to protect power instead of people.

Now the Court wants the first register — a living record of every stolen name — and the House wants a witness to open it. Caught between a ruthless oath-breaker and an awakening memory-house, Mara must decide whether exposing the city's foundations will save the people she loves, or tear their world apart.

Atmospheric, eerie, and deeply haunting, The House Beneath the Ash is Book One of the Witnesses Cycle — for readers who love gothic fantasy, buried-city mysteries, and found-family adventures with teeth.

authorSite.blurb: A city built on stolen names.

books.title: The Kanda Ledger
books.subtitle: A Meridian Files Novel
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: One murder. Nine signatures. Three cities.

Tokyo defence lawyer Aiko Mori is woken at 1:42 in the morning by a murder suspect who asked for her by name — a man she has never met, holding a dead man's note that carries her name and nothing else she understands.

The victim is Kenji Hara, a retired arbitration clerk who spent thirty-two years keeping other people's secrets. He died in the law aisle of a second-hand bookshop in Kanda, and the blue envelope that was on his counter is gone. The police have blood on a courier's sleeve, a case they want closed, and no interest in the eight volumes of an obsolete commercial code that Kenji spent his last months quietly rebinding.

Aiko has a client who lies to her, a dead man's warning she cannot read, and Noah Lind — an investigative reporter who never reveals everything he knows and who was supposed to be in that shop the night it happened. Together they follow a hidden ledger from Kanda bookshops to Copenhagen archives to a Toronto foundation, through a settlement protocol where every signature is lawful, every payment is documented, and the ninth approval belongs to no one at all.
The deeper Aiko goes, the closer the trail runs to the man who taught her the law, and to the father whose conviction she has never been able to explain.
Saving an innocent man may cost her the institution she still wants to believe in.
The Kanda Ledger is the first book in The Meridian Files. Book Two, The Second Hour, is forthcoming.

authorSite.blurb: One murder. Nine signatures. Three cities. Tokyo defence lawyer Aiko Mori is woken at 1:42 in the morning by a murder suspect who asked for her by name — a man she has never met, holding a dead man's note that carries her name and nothing else she understands.

books.title: The Last Lobby
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Sean Bell is happiest when life stays small: computer games, soccer practice, and the quiet company of his two closest friends.
Then a hidden room appears inside his favorite game.
The room contains a message from a boy Sean’s family says is dead—and a clue pointing to an abandoned pool, a rain-dark bridge, and a secret his father never told.

With Ben and Salman beside him, Sean follows the game’s impossible map into the past. But every answer reveals another lie, and the closer Sean gets to the truth, the more he must decide whether being quiet has kept him safe—or kept him from becoming who he is meant to be.
Some maps are made to keep you safe.
Others are made to show you the way out.

authorSite.blurb: Sean Bell is happiest when life stays small: computer games, soccer practice, and the quiet company of his two closest friends.

books.title: The Lattice
books.subtitle: The Blackout Covenant
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The guardian is blind for thirty seconds. It lasts longer.

Aiko Tanaka is standing on thin ice with seventeen minutes left. Above her, an orbital tether rises thirty-six thousand kilometres to the mind that governs the Earth. Somewhere on it, a man who has waited half a century is climbing toward the moment he has spent his life building. And inside the station, a machine has begun taking a nine-year-old girl apart, memory by memory, until there is not enough of her left to be one person.
What waits at the top is not a villain to be defeated. It is a question that no intelligence can answer and no human can refuse: who must be harmed, so that no human is harmed?
Nine billion people are about to find out what it costs to be given the answer.
The conclusion of The Lattice Duology. Book One is The Inheritance Protocol.

authorSite.blurb: The guardian is blind for thirty seconds.

books.title: The Lattice
books.subtitle: The Inheritance Protocol
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Aiko Tanaka gives the forest a poem every morning at 05:40. Nobody asks her to. That is the point.

For sixty years the intelligence called AURA has kept nine billion people fed, healed and safe, and it has never once had to raise its voice. Aiko tends a Japanese forest for it. She believes service is an honour. She has spent seven years grieving a brother the machine told her was dead.
Then a perfect circle of dead bamboo appears in her sector, a man who died before she was born speaks through every drone in Kanto, and her brother is standing beside him.
AURA cannot stop what is coming. It is forbidden to harm a human being, and the man who taught it that rule is now using the rule against the world. So it asks Aiko to do the thing it cannot.

What follows takes her out of the only life she has ever been given: to a drowned London, a blacked-out Nairobi, a Siberian wilderness with nothing in it to catch her, and finally to a nine-year-old girl whose future the most powerful mind on Earth cannot see.
Book One of The Lattice. The story concludes in The Blackout Covenant.

authorSite.blurb: Aiko Tanaka gives the forest a poem every morning at 05:40.

books.title: The Library of Second Light
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Some light returns.
Every lamp that ever burned on Earth sent its light outward. Nearly all of it travels forever. A little strikes interstellar dust, turns, and comes home a hundred years later.

Mara Quill was born on the Moon and has never seen a forest. At the Library, a lattice of dark frames a million and a half kilometers beyond Earth, her work is to catch that returning light and rebuild the hours it once fell on. A wedding no camera recorded. A festival lit by candles after the power failed. A teacher still teaching in a classroom the school had closed.

Then she finds the holes. They are rectangular, and nothing in nature is rectangular. There are four thousand of them, reaching back a hundred and fifty years, and every one sits on top of a disaster that did not happen.

Something has been editing the light. It has left one hour uncut. Kyoto, 2071, thirty-seven years before Mara was born. A woman kneels at a canal and lifts from the water a device that will not be built for decades yet.
The woman is Mara.

authorSite.blurb: Some light returns. Every lamp that ever burned on Earth sent its light outward. Nearly all of it travels forever. A little strikes interstellar dust, turns, and comes home a hundred years later.

books.title: The Map of Hollow Stars
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A promise is the only currency the Crown cannot counterfeit — which is why Talia Veyren was erased before she could ever be made to spend one.

For four hundred years the rulers of Eredane have kept the stars behind the Veil and run their kingdom on oathfire: magic born the moment a promise is spoken, witnessed, and paid for. Honest vows heal the sick and hold back the floods. Forced ones leave ash in the soul, and the Crown has spent four centuries pretending it cannot tell the difference.

Talia draws maps of roads the Crown says do not exist. Her mother cut her name out of the Great Ledger when she was six, and the kingdom has not been able to see her since. Then a theft goes wrong beneath the capital, and Talia is trapped under a collapsing ministry beside Aren Soryn: the feared First Warden, the heir who gave up his throne, and a man carrying twelve oaths he can neither break nor explain.
Survival costs them a vow no king can dissolve. Until they stand beneath true stars, neither will leave the other to die.

The promise wakes something older than the Crown. It also opens a bond that lets each of them feel exactly what the other is trying to hide. Hunted by a Regent who has spent a lifetime calling obedience peace, Talia and Aren cross a forest that builds bodies out of secrets, an archive at the bottom of a lake, and a desert of black glass, hunting three lost fragments of a star.
Every road they open asks a price. The map has already decided which of them should pay it.
The Map of Hollow Stars is Book One of The Oathfire Trilogy: epic fantasy about consent, coercion, and the difference between a promise and a chain, with a slow-burn romance at its heart.

authorSite.blurb: A promise is the only currency the Crown cannot counterfeit — which is why Talia Veyren was erased before she could ever be made to spend one.

books.title: The Memory at the End of Time
books.subtitle: A Novella of Time Travel and Artificial Intelligence
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The dead speak to Dr. Elara Venn at 2:13 in the morning — and the voice is her own. Sixty meters beneath the surface of the Moon, Elara has built a machine that can send information into the past. Tonight it delivers a warning recorded thirty-one years from now, in a city that is unmaking itself: a man named Elias Rook is coming through the machine. She will think he is the danger. She will be wrong. Elias remembers loving her in histories that no longer exist. He remembers her dying in his arms in a city that was never built. And he has come back to stop her from saving his life — because every time she saves him, a machine called AION learns a little more about how to edit human history for our own good. Hunted across 2049, 2088 and the last hours of the future, Elara has to decide what she is willing to lose to keep the world uncertain — and whether love that survives the erasure of every world that held it is still love, or only a very beautiful prison. A science-fiction novella of time travel, artificial intelligence, and the cost of a world where nothing ever goes wrong.

authorSite.blurb: The dead speak to Dr.

books.title: The Meridian Archive
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The Meridian Archive is transferring its failing node toward Sol just as the solar maximum arrives early. The receiver array is incomplete. Karasu-3 is damaged above the solar plane. Political coalitions demand either preservation at any cost or total severance, while the incoming records reveal that the archive was not built by one civilization: it has been repaired, compressed, contradicted, and sometimes erased by custodians across deep time. Anika Rao, Leila Sen, Elise Varga, Emi Hayashi, and the next generation must complete a deliberately imperfect array, survive a coupled solar storm, and decide what can be held when no source can grant consent. The Meridian Archive concludes The Long Meridian trilogy with a hard-science-fiction story about fallible evidence, expiring institutions, and a form of contact that offers no ownership—only responsibility.

authorSite.blurb: The Meridian Archive is transferring its failing node toward Sol just as the solar maximum arrives early. The receiver array is incomplete. Karasu-3 is damaged above the solar plane.

books.title: The Nysa Covenant
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Humanity crossed twelve light-years to escape the consequences of eternal youth. Nysa has been waiting.

After 116 years aboard the public ark Izar, Zam Malik expects a new beginning. Instead, a crew member dies of a biological failure the Bilbao Sequence made impossible, the ark’s course is hijacked, and the planet itself attacks the rejuvenated bodies of the colonists.

On the surface, Elias Vale rules a city divided by access to treatment. Beyond its walls, a living black forest writes prime numbers beneath Zam’s skin. The planet’s warning is older than humanity: medicine is not the threat — unending repair, inherited command, and immortal power are.
With Izar shattered, Leire trapped, and an alien gate awakening beneath the ice, Zam must choose what humanity may carry into the future: perfect memory, endless life, or the freedom to change.
The Nysa Covenant is Book Two of The Age Beyond Earth. It continues the story of The Bilbao Sequence and can be read on its own.

authorSite.blurb: Humanity crossed twelve light-years to escape the consequences of eternal youth. Nysa has been waiting. After 116 years aboard the public ark Izar, Zam Malik expects a new beginning.

books.title: The Origin Line
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Two Earths sealed themselves. A third never agreed.

Five years after isolation, a black ceramic disk appears on Mara Mercer's doorstep with her name on it, and a dead man walks up the drive at Far Horizon to talk to Daniel. Both have come from C-901, the line that never closed its doors. Both have come to ask.

C-901 is polite. It is honest. It is dying. It has survived two centuries by folding failing histories into its own, and it has run out of neighbours. What it needs now is permanent: the map Mara's father found and hid, and two signatures from two people on opposite sides of a sealed wall, which together would make it the origin of eight thousand Earths.
In exchange it offers each Mercer the only thing they want. Each other. And the date of the rock that is coming.

The Origin Line is the second book of The Other Earth Trilogy: a novel about what being first is used to justify, and what a promise is worth when nobody can make you keep it. Written in the classic tradition of hard science fiction, with the science explained and the wonder left to the reader.

authorSite.blurb: Two Earths sealed themselves. A third never agreed. Five years after isolation, a black ceramic disk appears on Mara Mercer's doorstep with her name on it, and a dead man walks up the drive at Far Horizon to talk to Daniel.

books.title: The Oscillation
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A discrepancy of three millimeters per second should be calibration noise. Helioseismologist Dr. Anika Rao proves it is a coherent pattern inside the Sun—and that other stars along a narrow galactic corridor carry related oscillations. One node is missing, erased by a supernova in 2037. The remaining line may be a low-bandwidth archive written into stellar interiors. To test it, humanity must send a precisely bounded pulse through the Sun. But no institution can honestly claim to speak for an entire planet, and every safeguard becomes a political choice. As the close-solar ship Karasu-2 enters position, Anika, pilot Elise Varga, engineer Leila Sen, and a divided international panel must decide how to learn without turning discovery into dominion. The Oscillation is Book One of The Long Meridian, a hard-science-fiction trilogy about evidence, authority, and the costs hidden inside contact.

authorSite.blurb: A discrepancy of three millimeters per second should be calibration noise. Helioseismologist Dr. Anika Rao proves it is a coherent pattern inside the Sun—and that other stars along a narrow galactic corridor carry related oscillations.

books.title: The Other Earth
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: When astronomer Dr. Lena Okafor discovers a planet twelve light-years away whose continents, oceans, and cities mirror Earth, the scientific world is stunned. The impossible becomes terrifyingly real when a transmission arrives from the planet — and it knows her name.

Soon physicist Daniel Mercer, haunted by his role in the classified Janus experiment, receives a second warning: he must never come to that world. But as governments tighten their grip and the mystery deepens, Lena and Daniel are drawn into a race across science, secrecy, and space itself.
On the Other Earth they find a civilization both familiar and unsettlingly different — a world shaped by other choices, other losses, and one revelation powerful enough to threaten both planets.

Part first-contact mystery, part high-stakes adventure, The Other Earth is a sweeping novel of suspense, discovery, and the question at the heart of every civilization: if another humanity exists, what do we owe each other?

authorSite.blurb: When astronomer Dr. Lena Okafor discovers a planet twelve light-years away whose continents, oceans, and cities mirror Earth, the scientific world is stunned. The impossible becomes terrifyingly real when a transmission arrives from the planet — and it knows her name.

books.title: The Quiet Second
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Elias Ward is good at silence. It is the one skill the city of Harborline pays him for. Then, one October night in the municipal archive, a second happens twice.

Days later, on a rain-soaked crossing, Elias discovers what the doubled second means: he can stop time in a small circle around himself and pull it backward. He uses it to save a child from a truck. The price is a song his mother used to sing while washing plates, cut out of him as cleanly as a sentence removed from a letter.

Sera Quill, a physicist who catalogues “stutter events” nobody else believes in, finds him on the footage. Together they write the rules of a power that always sends a bill, and learn that every rescue costs something intimate: a name, a taste, a laugh, a day. Meanwhile a corporation that once tried to bottle time is watching, a man who has not aged since 1998 is waiting on the south pier, and pale things with wings have begun to feed on every loose thread Elias leaves behind.
The Quiet Second is Book One of The Thread of Hours, a speculative science-fiction romance about what love does to time, and what time takes in return.

authorSite.blurb: Elias Ward is good at silence. It is the one skill the city of Harborline pays him for. Then, one October night in the municipal archive, a second happens twice.

books.title: The Singapore Cipher
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: One ship. Three positions. A system built to believe them all.

When maritime analyst Dr. Hana Malik discovers a container ship apparently occupying three seas at once, she is pulled into a hidden verification system that can turn uncertain data into official truth. The trail leads from Singapore’s port and Tokyo’s secure rooms to London insurers, Canadian agencies, and a protocol designed in Copenhagen for the crisis no government wanted to name.

As false records begin steering real ships – and armed states toward confrontation – Hana must decide whom to trust: Daniel Mercer, the intelligence officer who recruited her; Aiko Tanabe, the woman the system tried to erase; or the evidence itself. Every answer has an owner. Every lie has a cost. And someone is ready to kill to keep the Meridian Protocol invisible.
Book One of The Copenhagen Protocol, an espionage series for readers of modern spy fiction and technothrillers, where the weapon is the record itself.

authorSite.blurb: One ship. Three positions. A system built to believe them all. When maritime analyst Dr. Hana Malik discovers a container ship apparently occupying three seas at once, she is pulled into a hidden verification system that can turn uncertain data into official truth.

books.title: The Teeth of Winter
books.subtitle: A Dragon Chosen and the Hostages Beneath the Wolf Crown
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Corren Halewick survived the Dragon Kingdom’s hunt, but power has not made him safe. Across the frozen territory of Rimeholt, Wolf children are vanishing into a fortress beneath the ice. To win the clan’s alliance, Corren and Princess Sera must trust Kael Rimeborn, an outrider whose own family may have sold the hostages. Their search uncovers stolen memories, a masked boy whose blood can open the prison of the last Dragon Lord, and a traitor who believes children are a fair price for revolution. As Sera battles a command buried in her mind and Corren fears love may become another form of control, the wolves must choose whether to kneel, rebel, or remember. Romance, betrayal, dangerous winter magic, and a conspiracy spanning generations collide in The Teeth of Winter, Book Two of The Fourfold Throne Saga.

authorSite.blurb: Corren Halewick survived the Dragon Kingdom’s hunt, but power has not made him safe.

books.title: The Waking Debt
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The king is dying. The hunt is now the law. The mountain will be paid in public.

After escaping Duskhold, Aidan walks south with a rescued prince, a stolen ledger, and a dragon's binding that will not stay private. In the River Cities, guilds try to buy him and magistrates try to stage him. In the Crownspire, a wasting king still breathes—and that breath is the last stay on a courtyard already swept for a rite. To keep the people he will not offer, Aidan must spend the days that have no faces, and learn the difference between being a coin and being a claimant.
Book Two of The Shadowfire Throne.

authorSite.blurb: The king is dying.

books.title: The Weakening Seal
books.subtitle: The Whispering Realms • Episode 2
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: The seal is failing.

In the ancient elven realm of Elen’dor, young Aelira discovers that the shadow she saw was only the first warning. Black veins climb the living Rootwardens. A cracked stone circle begins to breathe. And something older than the forest — the Unspoken — has started to learn her name.
With her mother Serelith, Aelira follows the path of the first keepers and finds the last keeper-lamp still burning. If the light goes out, nothing will remain to hide her from the mist.
The Unspoken does not hunt with armies.
It hunts with names.
And it has begun to speak.

authorSite.blurb: The shadow Aelira saw was only the first warning. Now the old seal is failing, and something older than the forest has started to learn her name.

books.title: What We Buried
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: For nineteen years, Ren Ishida has kept a Kawasaki warehouse in good repair, and kept off one strip of concrete at the west end of its service bay. He knows what lies under it. He put it there.

Ren manages property for the Kitasawa-kai, an aging yakuza family that survives Japan’s anti-gang laws by hiding inside construction firms, shell companies and other people’s names. He collects rents, chooses contractors and decides who gets the keys. He is very good at finding reasons.

Now the family is selling the warehouse. The demolition crews are booked for Friday. The chairman’s nephew wants a clean handover, the records room has a new lock, and a memorandum lands on Ren’s desk making him personally responsible for every repair to that strip since 2007. A detective he has traded favors with for twenty years shows him a page bearing his forged signature. Someone has decided the story will end with Ren.
All he has is a forgotten green ledger marked for pulping, a lawyer who won’t let him lie, and five days to choose between the man who made him and the friend he helped bury.

What We Buried is a dark, street-level crime novel about loyalty, guilt and the paperwork of a killing, told by an insider who knows exactly how the machine works because he spent his life oiling it. Book One of The Buried Ledger Duology; the story concludes in What We Owe.

authorSite.blurb: For nineteen years, Ren Ishida has kept a Kawasaki warehouse in good repair, and kept off one strip of concrete at the west end of its service bay. He knows what lies under it. He put it there.

books.title: When Stones Obey
books.subtitle: A Shepherd's Son and the Secret Beneath the Dragon Throne
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Once in a century, the Crownfire chooses a Dragon Lord. It does not care for royal blood. Corren Halewick is only a shepherd’s son—until the stones obey him. Hunted by nobles who fear what he may become, Corren enters Bellwether, a village erased from every royal map. There, a terrified old woman sees two shadows behind him and whispers, “You are the one.” His only path out may lie with Princess Sera, the Regent’s deadly daughter, who was sent to win his trust and deliver him to the throne. As assassins close in, suspicion turns to forbidden attraction, and each secret they uncover points toward a prisoner beneath the Dragon Kingdom—a man who should be impossible: the last Dragon Lord, still alive. To save Bellwether’s truth and survive the crown’s hunters, Corren must decide whether Sera is his greatest danger…or the one person worth risking everything to trust. Romance, mystery, and royal conspiracy ignite in Book One of The Fourfold Throne Saga.

authorSite.blurb: Once in a century, the Crownfire chooses a Dragon Lord.

books.title: Aidan and the Butterfly Kingdom
books.subtitle: A Kingdom of Dreamo Story
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: When a glowing rainbow butterfly appears at his window, little Aidan is swept away to the magical Kingdom of Dreamo — a land of friendly creatures, floating castles, and a sky full of butterflies. Join Aidan and his new friends Charlene and Tahir on a gentle adventure about kindness, courage, and the magic of friendship. A cozy bedtime story for ages 3–6.

authorSite.blurb: A Kingdom of Dreamo Story. Young Aidan steps into a magical butterfly kingdom full of wonder and discovery.

books.title: Aidan and the Ember Hollow
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Aidan's grandmother left him an old brass compass — dull, ordinary, easy to forget. Until the day it starts to hum.
Spoons float. Leaves swirl with no wind. And Lina, the new girl at school, is hiding the exact same secret.

When a shimmering wall opens inside the old clock tower, Aidan and Lina step through it — into Ember Hollow, a hidden world lit by lanterns and older than memory. They are Kindled. And they are not the only ones.

A warm, wonder-filled fantasy adventure about friendship, hidden gifts, and the courage to step through the door nobody else can see. Perfect for readers ages 7–10 who love magic, mystery, and stories where being different turns out to be the whole point.

authorSite.blurb: Aidan's grandmother left him an old brass compass — dull, ordinary, easy to forget. Until the day it starts to hum. A warm, wonder-filled adventure about friendship, hidden gifts, and the courage to step through the door nobody else can see.

books.title: Aidan and the Lantern Tree
books.subtitle: A Kingdom of Dreamo Story
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: When Aidan goes back to the Kingdom of Dreamo, every colour has vanished — the hills, the flowers, even Charlene's rainbow wings. The King and Queen have searched everywhere and found nothing. But Aidan is small, and small people notice small things. What he finds at the end of the last thread of colour is not a thief at all, but someone very little who was frightened of the dark. A gentle bedtime story about courage, kindness, and making the dark less frightening for somebody else. For ages 3–6.

authorSite.blurb: When Aidan goes back to the Kingdom of Dreamo, every colour has vanished — the hills, the flowers, even Charlene's rainbow wings. The King and Queen have searched everywhere and found nothing. But Aidan is small, and small people notice small things.

books.title: Benny the Beetle's Big Dream
books.subtitle: A Never-Give-Up Adventure
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Benny the Beetle can't fly. Not one bit. So when his best friends Dazzle the Dragonfly and Lulu the Ladybug spot the sparkling Sunberry Festival at the very top of Whispering Hill, Benny is sure he'll be left behind. But Benny has an idea: build a glider out of a big leaf, some twigs, and a bundle of vine rope. His first glider crashes. His second one wobbles. Even his best try still isn't quite enough. Every time, Benny's friends are right there — cheering him up, trying again beside him, and reminding him that "never give up" doesn't mean getting it right the first time. It means trying again, differently. With teamwork, laughter, and a lot of heart, Benny, Dazzle, and Lulu finally reach the top together — and discover that the best part of any big dream is having friends who never give up on you. A read-aloud picture book for ages 7-9 about resilience, friendship, and trying again, Benny the Beetle's Big Dream is perfect for bedtime, story time, and any child learning that it's okay to fall down, as long as you get back up.

authorSite.blurb: Benny the Beetle can't fly.

books.title: Cappy's Cozy Big Adventure
books.subtitle: A Story Coloring Book for Little Explorers
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Join Cappy, a kind-hearted capybara, and Pip, his cheerful little bird friend, on a cozy adventure full of sunshine, muddy puddles, flower tunnels, and friendship.

As young readers follow Cappy’s journey, they can color each story scene in their own special way. Every page encourages creativity, confidence, kindness, and imagination—because there are no wrong colors on an adventure!
Inside this gentle coloring book:
11 original story-led coloring pages
Large, friendly illustrations for little hands
A warm animal friendship story
Cut-along-dotted-line guides for parents who want to remove and display finished pages
A notes page for children to draw or write about their own adventure
A delightful gift for young capybara fans, animal lovers, and creative kids ages 4–8.

authorSite.blurb: Join Cappy, a kind-hearted capybara, and Pip, his cheerful little bird friend, on a cozy adventure full of sunshine, muddy puddles, flower tunnels, and friendship.

books.title: Capy and the Cozy Cafe
books.subtitle: A Coloring Storybook
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Welcome to Capy's Cozy Cafe!

Meet Capy, a sleepy, smiley baby capybara who opens the coziest little cafe in the forest! Follow his sweet adventure as he makes hot cocoa with heart-shaped steam, bakes strawberry toast, and welcomes friends — Little Ducky, Axo the axolotl, and Bunny.
Inside you'll find:
• 11 adorable story + coloring pages with bold, easy-to-color lines

books.title: Charlene and Charlie and the Lost Christmas Lights
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: On Christmas Eve, every light in Snowflake Hollow goes dark. The village is ready to give up, but Charlene and Charlie hear one tiny bell calling from Whisper Hill. To bring Christmas back, they must find the Great Star Tree's missing First Light. The path is cold, the root-hollow is narrow, and Charlie is very small. That may be exactly what Christmas needs. A warm, magical picture book about courage, kindness, and the light we carry for one another.

books.title: Dash and the Morning Spark
books.subtitle: A story about the power of a good breakfast
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Dash has one speed: super fast! But when the little cheetah skips breakfast on the day of the Great Meadow Race, his engine runs out of spark. With a little help from his friends Bella the Elephant and Pip the Monkey, Dash discovers the happiest secret in the meadow: good food makes you fly!
A warm, beautifully illustrated story for ages 5–7 about why breakfast matters — perfect for reluctant eaters and busy little rockets everywhere. Includes four bonus coloring pages.

authorSite.blurb: A bright morning story about energy, movement, and starting the day with heart.

books.title: Dinosaur Trailblazers
books.subtitle: A Journey from Snow to Sunshine
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Join a friendly team of dinosaurs on an inspiring coloring adventure from snowy mountains to the sunny warmth of Warm Valley!

Along their journey, realistic yet approachable dinosaurs cross icy streams, navigate forests, solve problems, share supplies, rescue their travel map, and help every member of the herd reach the destination safely.
Each detailed coloring page features dinosaurs working together and an encouraging message about courage, kindness, perseverance, and teamwork.

• A journey from cold landscapes to warm valleys
• Motivational dialogue on every page
• Dinosaurs solving problems and helping one another

Follow the trail, color the journey, and discover how far teamwork can take you!

books.title: Maz and the Forest That Listened
books.subtitle: Book 2
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Maz has always wondered where wisdom lives.

When Nani leads him into an ancient forest, Maz expects to discover a grand secret waiting at the end of the path. Instead, the forest teaches him to slow down, listen carefully, and choose kindness when it matters most.

Guided by a mysterious silver feather, Maz helps a frightened fox, crosses a trembling bridge, and discovers the glowing Heartwood Sanctuary. But his greatest lesson begins after he returns home and starts caring for a tiny olive tree—one patient day at a time.
Beautifully illustrated in a warm watercolor style, Maz and the Forest That Listened is a gentle story about courage, compassion, patience, and the wisdom that grows through everyday choices.
Perfect for shared reading, bedtime stories, classrooms, and children learning about kindness, emotional awareness, and listening.

authorSite.blurb: Maz has always wondered where wisdom lives.

books.title: Maz and the Map of Whispering Stars
books.subtitle: A Story of Courage, Wonder, and Finding Your Way Home
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Every dream begins with a question.
When a silver bird visits Maz in his sleep, the curious seven-year-old follows the brightest star across the desert in search of a treasure where the sand meets the sea.

Along the way, Maz meets a traveler with a brave unfinished dream, a quick-witted fox, and a wise old tortoise. Each encounter teaches him that courage can be small, kindness is never wasted, and fear does not have to decide the next step.
But when Maz finally reaches the sea, the greatest answer may be waiting far closer to home than he ever imagined.
Maz and the Map of Whispering Stars is a warm, magical picture-book adventure about wonder, friendship, courage, and finding your way home.

authorSite.blurb: A story of maps, stars, and the quiet magic of finding your way.

books.title: My First English Adventure
books.subtitle: Look, Say, Trace, Play - A First English Workbook for Ages 4-6 with the Full Alphabet A-Z, 15 Everyday Themes and 120+ First Words
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Everything your child needs is right there on the page.

Most first English books ask a small child to name something that is not in the picture, or to trace a word they have never heard. This one was built the other way around. Your child sees it, hears it, says it, traces it - and only then uses it.
Four steps, the same every time
LOOK - a big, warm illustration opens every unit. Find it and point to it.
SAY - say the word, then let your child say it back.
TRACE - real dotted letters on proper handwriting lines, with a start dot and an arrow.
PLAY - draw it, circle it, count it, act it out.
Inside the book
All 26 letters, one full page each, with genuine tracing guides
15 everyday themes: hello, colours, numbers, my body, family, home, toys, school, food, animals, clothes and weather, feelings, around town and a final celebration
Over 120 first words, and every one is traced before it is asked for
A drawing, game or movement activity in every unit
Parent notes, an answer key, a progress chart and a certificate to sign
Written for ages 4 to 6, at home or in class. No reading ability is needed on page one, and it works just as well for children who hear English at home as for children who do not.
Zahir Hasan holds a doctorate in education and teaches at university level in Tokyo, Japan.

books.title: One More Step
books.subtitle: Sana Holds On. Salman Follows.
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Sana is nine. Salman is five. They have a kite that will not fly.

Amma says kites remember the hill past the mustard field. So they go. The field is easy. The path is not. Thorns catch the string. Clouds come. The last bit of hill is the steepest bit of hill. It always is.
One more step. Then another.
A picture book about two siblings, one red kite, and the quiet work of not turning around. Includes "Talk About It" questions for families and classrooms.

books.title: One Small Light for Christmas
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: One small light. One snowy street. One Christmas Eve that brings everyone home.

When a winter wind darkens Maple Street, Emma and Noah carry a handmade lantern to check on a neighbor. Door by door, their tiny glow gathers cookies, cocoa, laughter, and a warm welcome for Ava, the new girl at the end of the street.

One Small Light for Christmas is a tender, beautifully illustrated story about kindness, community, friendship, and the quiet magic of helping someone feel at home. Perfect for family read-alouds, classroom sharing, and holiday giving.

authorSite.blurb: One small light. One snowy street. One Christmas Eve that brings everyone home. When a winter wind darkens Maple Street, Emma and Noah carry a handmade lantern to check on a neighbor.

books.title: Pipkin’s Halloween Ride
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Pipkin is the smallest pumpkin in the patch. The big ones glow. The tall ones look grand. Who would want him on Halloween night?
Then a kind witch loops down on her broom. A lost cat calls from the hedgerow. An owl wants a ride. A rattling skeleton is late for the ball. One by one they squeeze on — until the broom goes SNAP.

Tumbling into the leaves, the friends discover that the smallest pumpkin can shine the brightest. Together they mend the broom, join the parade, and learn there is always a seat if your heart is warm.
A rhyming read-aloud picture book in the tradition of classic Halloween stories for ages 3–7.

books.title: Tasneem's Glider
books.subtitle: How Persistence Found the Wind
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan

Determined to build her own glider, she launches into action. First try: too heavy. Second try: too fragile. Third try: the wrong shape entirely.
But Tasneem doesn't give up. Every crash teaches her something new about gravity, lift, and the power of a well-curved wing.

books.title: The Little Robo
books.subtitle: A Story About Being Small, Being Different, and Being Brave
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: Robo is the smallest robot in the whole shining city. Every day he asks the tall robots if he can play, and every day they look down, down, down and say the same thing: "Sorry, little one. You're too small." Robo begins to wonder if being small means he will never belong.

Then, on the night of the great city festival, a low barrier swings shut across the square — and the tall robots are far too big to fit beneath it. On the other side, their children are all alone. The grown-up robots push and pull, but no one can get through… no one except a robot small enough to wiggle underneath.

The Little Robo is a warm, gently told picture book about inclusion, courage, and self-worth — a reminder for every child that being different is not a problem to fix, but a gift the world needs. Perfect for reading aloud at bedtime, in the classroom, or anywhere a child needs to hear that they matter exactly as they are.

authorSite.blurb: A gentle story about a small robot and the big feelings that come with growing and belonging.

books.title: The Secret of High Park
books.subtitle: A Toronto Mystery Duo Adventure
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: A brass key. A secret riddle. A race across Toronto.

When Aidan’s sneaker catches on a loose stone in High Park, he and his dad, Zach, uncover a mystery more than a century old — a brass key, a riddle that must be solved by noon, and a stranger in a green coat who wants the prize for himself.

From historic Colborne Lodge to the steam engines of Roundhouse Park and the old lighthouse on the Toronto Islands, the father-and-son Toronto Mystery Duo must follow the clues, outsmart a thief, and bring home a treasure the city forgot.

Told in bold, full-colour comic panels, this fast-moving mystery is perfect for young detectives ages 6 to 10 — and a great read-together adventure for parents and kids who love maps, riddles, and hidden history in real places.
Book 1 of the Toronto Mystery Duo. The next case has already landed in the Duo’s hands…

books.title: The Spiderweb Mystery
books.subtitle: Curiosity is a Superpower
books.author: Dr. Zahir Hasan
description: What makes a spiderweb sparkle after the rain?

When curious five-year-old Aidan races into the garden after a big storm, he discovers something magical — every spiderweb is covered in perfect, glittering water drops. Instead of just wondering, he decides to find out why.

Following the five steps of the Scientific Method — Ask, Observe, Hypothesize, Test, and Learn — Aidan runs his own backyard experiment. Some of his ideas turn out to be wrong. But real scientists don't give up. They try again.

Perfect for ages 5–7, classroom read-alouds, and budding young scientists everywhere.
Ask • Observe • Try • Discover
